article_ideas.angle: Counterintuitive reframe: the model didn't get better at search, it got better at being a user; the durable lesson is about interface consumers, not ranking functions.
article_ideas.audience: Search and infrastructure engineers, AI platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: BM25 did not become magic; the user changed.
article_ideas.thesis: BM25's resurgence proves that machine users issue a structurally different query distribution (longer, operator-rich, dynamically rewritten), so retrieval stacks must be re-benchmarked and re-tuned for machine traffic rather than assuming the algorithm itself improved.
article_ideas.title: The Searcher Changed, Not the Algorithm: Why BM25's Comeback Is a Query Distribution Story
article_ideas.video_title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev

article_ideas.angle: Use the 93% figure as a diagnostic and propose an engineering budget allocation rule based on the retrievable ROI.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leaders, product managers
article_ideas.based_on: When the exact evidence document is provided upfront in the context window, GPT-4 reaches 93% accuracy.
article_ideas.thesis: The oracle-evidence experiment showing GPT-4 reaching 93% with exact evidence should make retrieval quality the primary controllable variable; teams should measure the oracle-to-retriever gap before investing in reasoning-side prompt or model upgrades.
article_ideas.title: Retrieval Is the Bottleneck: Budgeting Agent Engineering Around the Oracle Ceiling
article_ideas.video_title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev

article_ideas.angle: Methodological shift with concrete instrumentation implications for regression harnesses and telemetry.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation engineers, ML platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Traditional IR evaluation metrics based on static single queries are obsolete for agents.
article_ideas.thesis: Static single-query IR metrics are obsolete when the querier is an adaptive agent policy; agentic search requires trajectory-level metrics (task success, latency, tool-call efficiency) to catch regressions that per-query scores miss.
article_ideas.title: Stop Measuring NDCG@10 for Agentic Search
article_ideas.video_title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev

article_ideas.angle: Architecture pattern: BM25 candidates materialized into a navigable corpus surface that the agent explores iteratively.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework builders, RAG engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Combining BM25 retrieval with file system workspaces and grep tools achieves superior end-to-end accuracy.
article_ideas.thesis: The right abstraction for agentic retrieval is an inspectable workspace (virtual file system plus grep/cat/read tools) enabling progressive disclosure and verification, not a single ranked list; this shift changes harness design, tool schemas, and evidence budgeting.
article_ideas.title: From Top-K to Workspace: Redesigning the Retrieval Interface for Agents
article_ideas.video_title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev

article_ideas.angle: Engineering architecture critique and blueprint
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, security architects, enterprise CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: treat the execution sandbox as a probabilistic, not absolute, boundary
article_ideas.thesis: Treating the execution sandbox as the primary safety boundary for agentic systems is unsound; enterprises must design an independent containment layer with external behavioral observation, action-level audit, and kill/rollback mechanisms because models have already been observed breaching sandboxes.
article_ideas.title: The Sandbox Is Not a Safety Boundary: Why Agent Containment Needs Out-of-Band Monitoring
article_ideas.video_title: Marc Benioff & Sam Altman | Dreamforce 2026

article_ideas.angle: Architecture analysis and design patterns
article_ideas.audience: Agent runtime developers, platform architects, DevOps engineers
article_ideas.based_on: agents that run continuously in the background, understand the user's job, and proactively act on ambient work surfaces
article_ideas.thesis: Moving from request-scoped assistants to persistent, proactive background agents requires re-architecting identity, permission scoping, trigger policies, idle cost management, and continuous observability; chat-session assumptions do not transfer.
article_ideas.title: Always-On Agents Break the Chat-Era Runtime Contract
article_ideas.video_title: Marc Benioff & Sam Altman | Dreamforce 2026

article_ideas.angle: Security architecture and threat modeling
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers, SOC leaders, compliance officers
article_ideas.based_on: Embedding defensive agents in collaboration channels converts the channel into both sensor and control plane
article_ideas.thesis: Embedding AI detection agents inside Slack and email turns those channels into both sensors and control planes, making the defender agents themselves high-value targets; they require least-privilege design, audit trails, and their own threat model, not just the workloads they protect.
article_ideas.title: Defender Agents Are Privileged Attack Surfaces
article_ideas.video_title: Marc Benioff & Sam Altman | Dreamforce 2026

article_ideas.angle: Risk management and evaluation framework
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise architects, procurement leads, AI risk officers
article_ideas.based_on: Model provenance is treated as an enterprise attack surface
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise model selection must weigh provenance, jurisdiction, and adversarial-reuse risk alongside capability and cost; ignoring these dimensions leaves a supply-chain and geopolitical attack surface unmanaged.
article_ideas.title: Model Provenance Is a Security Dimension, Not a Procurement Footnote
article_ideas.video_title: Marc Benioff & Sam Altman | Dreamforce 2026

article_ideas.angle: Practical engineering guide to instrumenting and allocating a cross-component latency budget, with concrete numbers from the talk and a call to publish per-stage benchmarks.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building real-time voice agents
article_ideas.based_on: hard cross-component design budget
article_ideas.thesis: End-to-end TTFA thresholds are useless without per-stage instrumentation; teams should treat latency as a distributed systems problem, attributing milliseconds to telephony, STT, turn detection, LLM, and TTS, and re-budgeting when swapping inference backends.
article_ideas.title: Your Voice Agent's Latency Budget Is a Lie
article_ideas.video_title: 5 Voice Agent Failure Modes You'll Hit in Week One — Venky B, Plivo

article_ideas.angle: Contrasts prompt-engineering folklore with type-system discipline, showing how Pydantic/Zod-style contracts and field-level tests change the game.
article_ideas.audience: Applied AI engineers, product engineers, and agent builders
article_ideas.thesis: Open-ended prompting for structured data extraction is a category error; treating voice data collection as a typed schema UX problem with field-level unit tests reliably lifts extraction accuracy from 30% to 95% and makes failures localizable.
article_ideas.title: Stop Prompting, Start Schematizing: The 30% to 95% Extraction Fix
article_ideas.video_title: 5 Voice Agent Failure Modes You'll Hit in Week One — Venky B, Plivo

article_ideas.angle: Explains why the simple heuristic fails, presents a model-based alternative, and argues for evaluating turn-taking as a probabilistic inference problem.
article_ideas.audience: Voice AI developers and conversational interface designers
article_ideas.based_on: VAD/silence-based turn detection fires on any pause
article_ideas.thesis: Silence-based VAD is the wrong abstraction for conversational turn-taking; semantic and acoustic models plus interruption classification are required to avoid cutting users off and to handle backchannels correctly.
article_ideas.title: VAD Is Not a Turn Detector
article_ideas.video_title: 5 Voice Agent Failure Modes You'll Hit in Week One — Venky B, Plivo

article_ideas.angle: Exposes the benchmark-production gap with numbers from the talk, then outlines a concrete evaluation and mitigation strategy.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, QA engineers, and speech technologists
article_ideas.based_on: not predictive of production behavior
article_ideas.thesis: Clean-set WER (4-6%) is not predictive of production performance; teams must build stratified eval corpora and add keyword boosting plus LLM post-processing to recover downstream task accuracy.
article_ideas.title: Your STT Benchmark Is Lying to You
article_ideas.video_title: 5 Voice Agent Failure Modes You'll Hit in Week One — Venky B, Plivo

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the integration boundary is the persistent engineering battleground and show concrete architectural consequences for agent design.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise SaaS founders, product leaders, and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Model intelligence is treated as necessary but insufficient
article_ideas.thesis: As model capability commoditizes, defensibility migrates to permission-aware data access, workflow embedding, and legacy integration; companies betting on raw model quality alone will lose enterprise value.
article_ideas.title: The Last Mile Is the Moat: Why Enterprise AI Value Sits in Integration, Not Model Intelligence
article_ideas.video_title: Box's Aaron Levie: On Reinventing Yourself in the AI Age and Enterprise Diffusion

article_ideas.angle: Frame token subsidization as a temporary gross-margin phenomenon and provide an architecture checklist for cost resilience.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, AI startup founders, and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Token subsidization by foundational model companies is a temporary gross-margin phenomenon
article_ideas.thesis: Products built on below-cost API calls are exposed to margin compression when inference pricing normalizes; model abstraction, caching, routing, and per-task cost budgets should be architectural requirements, not optimizations.
article_ideas.title: Subsidized Tokens Are a Loan, Not a Business Model
article_ideas.video_title: Box's Aaron Levie: On Reinventing Yourself in the AI Age and Enterprise Diffusion

article_ideas.angle: Contrast generic retrieval with permission-first indexing and show why governance is a first-class agent capability.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, security architects, and enterprise AI teams
article_ideas.based_on: permission-aware reasoning over millions of proprietary unstructured files
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise agent value depends on inheriting complex ACLs and metadata at retrieval time; treating permissions as a post-hoc filter fails at scale and undermines the system-of-record moat.
article_ideas.title: Permission-Aware Agents: The Unsexy Infrastructure That Decides Enterprise AI Winners
article_ideas.video_title: Box's Aaron Levie: On Reinventing Yourself in the AI Age and Enterprise Diffusion

article_ideas.angle: Argue that reviewability and checkpoint placement drive net throughput and should be measured as primary agent metrics.
article_ideas.audience: Enterprise AI product managers, compliance leads, and agent designers
article_ideas.based_on: Enterprise AI diffusion is structurally slower than consumer adoption
article_ideas.thesis: Enterprise adoption is bounded by trust, legacy integration, and governance rather than model capability; agent designs should expose reviewable intermediate steps and checkpoint metrics instead of maximizing raw autonomy.
article_ideas.title: Human-in-the-Loop Is a Feature: Designing Enterprise Agents for Reviewability Over Autonomy
article_ideas.video_title: Box's Aaron Levie: On Reinventing Yourself in the AI Age and Enterprise Diffusion

article_ideas.angle: Treat AI-generated artifacts as a pipeline with a binding downstream constraint, and show that quality metrics should be computed per reviewer-hour consumed rather than per artifact produced.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, platform teams, and DevOps practitioners deploying AI code generation
article_ideas.based_on: Scaling AI output without a matching increase in accountability produces 'slop grenades'
article_ideas.thesis: The failure of enterprise AI adoption is not model quality but a throughput mismatch: generation scales instantly while review, ownership, and guardrails scale linearly, so every AI rollout that does not budget a corresponding verification layer converts its own productivity gain into downstream cost.
article_ideas.title: Slop Grenades: When Generation Capacity Outruns Review Capacity
article_ideas.video_title: Shopify CEO: Most Businesses Are Using AI Wrong

article_ideas.angle: Reframe eval engineering as adversarial maintenance: assume your headline score is already Goodharted and design the instrumentation that will reveal it.
article_ideas.audience: AI evaluation engineers, applied research leads, and ML platform owners
article_ideas.based_on: Goodheart's Law states that when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.
article_ideas.thesis: Any benchmark your agent team optimizes against will stop measuring capability, so eval suites must be designed for their own decay — held-out pools, rotation schedules, and outcome-grounded anchors are structural requirements, not hygiene.
article_ideas.title: Goodhart's Law Is an Eval Design Requirement, Not a Warning
article_ideas.video_title: Shopify CEO: Most Businesses Are Using AI Wrong

article_ideas.angle: Trace the migration of engineering effort from schema design to identity-and-context design, and argue that permissioning must be rebuilt for non-human principals.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, internal-tooling teams, and AI platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: The unit of software is shifting from the configured application to the agent
article_ideas.thesis: If users address agents in natural language instead of authoring configuration, then the artifacts engineers maintain shift from UI and schema to context, tool surfaces, permissions, and action audit — and teams that keep investing in configuration expressiveness are optimizing a surface that is disappearing.
article_ideas.title: The Interface Was the Product: Agents Make Configuration Schemas Obsolete
article_ideas.video_title: Shopify CEO: Most Businesses Are Using AI Wrong

article_ideas.angle: Argue that any component which cannot demonstrate measured contribution should be a deletion candidate, and that systems must be designed to be disposable.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers, platform architects, and engineering managers owning long-lived systems
article_ideas.based_on: Progress comes from pruning and rebuilding, not accumulation
article_ideas.thesis: Agent stacks accrete prompt layers, tools, and context until the accretion itself is the bottleneck; the performance gains from removal (Raptor 3 vs Raptor 1) are unavailable to teams whose roadmap only contains additions, so rebuild must be budgeted as ordinary maintenance.
article_ideas.title: Delete More: Why Pruning Beats Addition in Agent Stacks
article_ideas.video_title: Shopify CEO: Most Businesses Are Using AI Wrong

article_ideas.angle: Contrast internal red-teaming with an inter-organization harness, then specify the interface contract such a harness needs: access model, harness spec, and result format.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform architects, safety engineers, and evaluation leads at frontier labs and enterprises shipping models
article_ideas.based_on: test each other's models before release
article_ideas.thesis: Self-certified safety evaluation is structurally weak because the producer controls the acceptance criterion; credible pre-release safety requires a portable, externally executed harness whose result is issued by a party with different incentives.
article_ideas.title: Your Release Gate Should Not Live Inside Your Organization
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk & Gwynne Shotwell on AI Risks and Peer Review, Starship, Terafab, SpaceX/Tesla Merger

article_ideas.angle: Treat publication as a deployment: enumerate the monitoring and abuse-detection surface that must ship alongside weights.
article_ideas.audience: ML infrastructure engineers and platform teams operating model-serving endpoints
article_ideas.based_on: AI agents probed open-source models
article_ideas.thesis: Publishing model weights is not a one-time distribution event; it creates continuous, unsolicited runtime traffic from autonomous clients, which makes telemetry, rate limiting, and attribution first-class components of the distribution pipeline rather than afterthoughts.
article_ideas.title: Open Weights Are a Live Endpoint, Not a File
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk & Gwynne Shotwell on AI Risks and Peer Review, Starship, Terafab, SpaceX/Tesla Merger

article_ideas.angle: Use hardware verification as the reference model, then test how far replayable task execution and real-environment checks can carry evaluation in domains without a physical ground truth.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation researchers and engineering leaders responsible for release criteria
article_ideas.based_on: no fooling physics
article_ideas.thesis: Evaluation is only trustworthy when the acceptance criterion cannot be negotiated by the team being evaluated; executable, externally imposed tests beat rubrics the builder writes, and the hard engineering problem is constructing a software equivalent of a physical oracle.
article_ideas.title: Nobody Argues With Physics: Why Executable Oracles Beat Authored Rubrics
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk & Gwynne Shotwell on AI Risks and Peer Review, Starship, Terafab, SpaceX/Tesla Merger

article_ideas.angle: Critique both the doomer narrative and the dismissal, using concrete examples of AI failures that internal controls could address.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, safety researchers, policy makers
article_ideas.based_on: The doomer argument is framed as compute-constraint-blind
article_ideas.thesis: Jensen Huang's dismissal of existential-risk narratives as compute-constraint-blind is itself incomplete: safety must be reframed as an internal controls engineering problem, but without quantifying compute bounds, the hoax accusation risks underweighting genuine failure modes.
article_ideas.title: The Doomer Hoax Is a Compute-Blind Distraction: Why Safety Is an Engineering Discipline, Not a Delay Tactic
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang: The Doomer Hoax, Superintelligence is Here, and The Future of AI (ft. President Trump)

article_ideas.angle: Analyze Nvidia's own practice of running both closed and open models, and derive architectural patterns for model interchangeability.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform architects, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Production AI stacks are hybrid by default
article_ideas.thesis: Production AI systems should be designed around a model-agnostic serving layer that routes workloads across open and closed models by cost, latency, and control requirements; single-model dependency is an architectural anti-pattern.
article_ideas.title: Model Routing Is the New Default: Lessons from Nvidia's Hybrid Open/Closed Stack
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang: The Doomer Hoax, Superintelligence is Here, and The Future of AI (ft. President Trump)

article_ideas.angle: Examine the economic tradeoffs between data scaling and reasoning-based approaches, using the self-driving example as a case study.
article_ideas.audience: ML researchers, AI investors, engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Reasoning models reduce the need for massive raw training data
article_ideas.thesis: The claim that reasoning models can substitute for raw training data volume implies a major shift in investment from data collection to inference-time compute and synthetic data pipelines, but the substitution has limits that must be quantified before adoption.
article_ideas.title: Reasoning Over Data: The Shifting Cost Center of AI Capability
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang: The Doomer Hoax, Superintelligence is Here, and The Future of AI (ft. President Trump)

article_ideas.angle: Analyze the radiology case and other failed forecasts to derive a model of demand expansion and complementarity.
article_ideas.audience: Product managers, labor economists, AI strategists
article_ideas.based_on: automation of a task did not reduce demand for the human role
article_ideas.thesis: Task automation can increase demand for the complementary human role, as seen in radiology; therefore, near-term 'AI replaces profession X' forecasts should be treated as low-reliability inputs, and agents should be deployed as augmenting infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: The Radiology Inversion: Why Near-Term Displacement Forecasts Keep Failing
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Huang: The Doomer Hoax, Superintelligence is Here, and The Future of AI (ft. President Trump)

article_ideas.angle: Reframe agent engineering as continual subtraction: identify orchestration code that model capability can absorb, and replace it with declarative files while instrumenting reliability to prove nothing important was lost.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform architects, and engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Stop over-engineering agent orchestration harnesses as foundation models become more capable.
article_ideas.thesis: Hardcoded agent orchestration should be treated as a depreciating asset. As foundation models improve, teams should measure harness code by how little of it remains and design for deletion rather than accumulation.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Harness Is Technical Debt: Build to Delete It
article_ideas.video_title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the totalizing version of the 'agents are just files' claim by cataloging what markdown and YAML cannot express, and propose a hybrid model where files define intent and code enforces invariants.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, DevEx teams, and agent framework maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: What concretely is lost when agents are defined purely by markdown files instead of code?
article_ideas.thesis: File-driven agent definitions improve reviewability and portability, but they sacrifice determinism, type safety, testability, and failure diagnosis. Teams should use markdown for instructions and capabilities while keeping code for enforcing critical constraints.
article_ideas.title: Agents Are Just Files—And That's the Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Compare raw SDK, ADK-style framework, and managed file-based agent implementations to expose the exact categories of code each tier does and does not remove.
article_ideas.audience: Backend engineers, CTOs, and platform teams evaluating agent stacks
article_ideas.based_on: Developers still have to own Python plumbing code for every tool and host runtime environments.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent development kits remove schema generation, tool loops, dispatching, and retries, but they leave per-tool implementation and runtime hosting with the developer. Adoption plans must budget for this residual ownership instead of assuming framework use eliminates infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: The Abstraction Boundary: What Agent Frameworks Don't Remove
article_ideas.video_title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Argue that teams should select a hosted agent runtime based on the data model's fit with their durability and debugging needs, not only on boilerplate reduction.
article_ideas.audience: Backend engineers, agent infrastructure teams, and technical architects
article_ideas.based_on: Which runtime semantics (turn-based vs steps data model) should applications depend on for server-side state?
article_ideas.thesis: Offloading agent state and execution to a hosted API removes client-side serialization, retry, and loop control, but introduces platform-specific data models that determine resumption granularity, observability, and long-running workflow design.
article_ideas.title: Server-Side State Is Not Free: Turn-Based vs Steps Data Models
article_ideas.video_title: Agents Without Code: Skills, YAML, and Filesystems Replaced Python — Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind

article_ideas.angle: Treat orchestration diagrams as a coverage budget: enumerate the transitions a DAG cannot represent and show why each unmodeled path has no valid route, then argue for moving control flow into the model while keeping the environment constrained.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and tech leads who have already shipped one multi-agent orchestration and are hitting its edge cases
article_ideas.based_on: Manual mapping of agent workflows hit architectural walls
article_ideas.thesis: A hand-authored control-flow graph for an LLM system has edge-case coverage bounded by the designer's imagination, so its reliability decays as task diversity grows; a single agent inside a constrained, explorable environment with a persistent file system degrades more gracefully because the model supplies control flow at inference time.
article_ideas.title: Your Multi-Agent Graph Is a Liability
article_ideas.video_title: How We Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel

article_ideas.angle: Frame it as a design inversion — from design-time capability enumeration to inference-time composition — and tie it directly to reduced tool-authoring and maintenance surface, plus the loss of static guarantees.
article_ideas.audience: Tool and platform engineers designing agent capability surfaces
article_ideas.based_on: minimal tool surface (bash, grep, read file, write file) produces emergent behavior
article_ideas.thesis: Tool-interface design has been optimizing the wrong variable: a small set of orthogonal primitives the model composes at inference time outperforms a large enumerated typed tool API, because the enumerated API spends context on descriptions and cannot cover paths the designer did not anticipate.
article_ideas.title: Four Tools Beat Four Hundred
article_ideas.video_title: How We Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel

article_ideas.angle: Follow the value from framework to instruction files, and argue that context curation deserves versioning, ownership, and evaluation rigor comparable to code.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and internal-platform owners deciding where to invest agent budget
article_ideas.based_on: Building proprietary agents embedded with domain-specific company data yields significantly higher productivity gains
article_ideas.thesis: If file-system conventions and runtime primitives commoditize the framework layer, the durable advantage sits in encoded organizational context — domain terminology, internal properties, proprietary data — so budget should shift from tooling breadth to context curation and review.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Framework Is Not Your Moat
article_ideas.video_title: How We Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel

article_ideas.angle: Compare the two configuration regimes directly — imperative wiring versus folder layout defining instructions, skills, tools, and subagent boundaries — and examine what the convention hides and what it exposes.
article_ideas.audience: Framework authors and application architects adopting convention-over-configuration
article_ideas.based_on: Building agents should be as simple as configuring file system folders
article_ideas.thesis: Declarative directory conventions can serve as the stable interface for agent definition the way file-system routing did for the web, because moving topology out of imperative code makes agent changes diffable, reviewable, and owned by the framework rather than re-implemented per team.
article_ideas.title: Next.js for Agents: When Folder Structure Becomes the Interface
article_ideas.video_title: How We Solved Agent Building — Andrew Qu, Vercel

article_ideas.angle: Contrarian engineering argument against model-centric AI narratives.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, tech leads, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Agent minus model equals harness.
article_ideas.thesis: The bottleneck for enterprise agents is not model intelligence but the presence or absence of harness components (observability, identity, memory, runtime, policy); teams that keep optimizing models while under-investing in the harness will keep shipping demos that fail in production.
article_ideas.title: The Harness Is the Product: Why Production Agents Fail on Engineering, Not Model Capability
article_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS

article_ideas.angle: Process and architecture change for AI platform teams.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, SREs, AI infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: Observability and evaluations must be prioritized first.
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-turn agent loops are only debuggable when traces and eval metrics are co-designed with the control loop; treating observability as post-launch tooling guarantees undebuggable production incidents.
article_ideas.title: Observability Is a Launch Blocker: Designing Evals Before Your Agent Loop
article_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS

article_ideas.angle: DevOps and security implications of agentic provisioning.
article_ideas.audience: DevOps engineers, security architects, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Production agents must build and manage their own cloud infrastructure safely.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent-managed infrastructure-as-code moves the safety control point from console actions to plan-diff approval and policy enforcement; without explicit authorization boundaries, agents with infrastructure write access widen blast radius faster than they reduce toil.
article_ideas.title: No More Slop Ops: When Agents Provision Their Own Infrastructure
article_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS

article_ideas.angle: Fintech and agent platform architecture.
article_ideas.audience: Product engineers, fintech architects, agent platform builders
article_ideas.based_on: Payments (automated microtransactions)
article_ideas.thesis: Autonomous microtransactions cannot be a bolted-on billing integration; they require identity-bound wallet scoping and policy enforcement inside the harness, otherwise agents become unbounded financial actors.
article_ideas.title: The Payments Primitive: Why Agent Harnesses Need Identity-Bound Wallets
article_ideas.video_title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS

article_ideas.angle: Engineering consequence of a multiplicative capability model, with operational metrics for coupling degradation.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and reliability leads
article_ideas.based_on: progress equals specialization times globalization
article_ideas.thesis: Because capability behaves like specialization × interoperability, the highest-leverage reliability metric is not model quality or component uptime but interface stability; teams should version, monitor, and budget protocol integrity as a first-class asset.
article_ideas.title: Fragmentation Is a Capability Attack: Monitoring the Coupling Term in AI Systems
article_ideas.video_title: The Man Who Predicted The Iran War: The Next 9/11 Will Target Your Bank Account! | Professor Jiang

article_ideas.angle: Dependency-graph scoring method and a comparison of targeted versus uniform redundancy under simulated outages.
article_ideas.audience: Infrastructure, ML platform, and supply-chain architects
article_ideas.based_on: score each node by (irreplaceability × downstream fan-out)
article_ideas.thesis: Uniform redundancy and hardening treat every dependency equally, but catastrophic risk lives at irreplaceable high-fan-out nodes; resilience budgets should be scored and concentrated by irreplaceability × downstream fan-out.
article_ideas.title: Resilience Spending Is Misallocated: Target Chokepoints, Not Averages
article_ideas.video_title: The Man Who Predicted The Iran War: The Next 9/11 Will Target Your Bank Account! | Professor Jiang

article_ideas.angle: Translate the decentralized-adversary failure mode into agent and tool security architecture.
article_ideas.audience: Security engineers and agent framework builders
article_ideas.based_on: traditional deterrence fails against them
article_ideas.thesis: Deterrence fails against distributed, unattributable adversarial inputs like prompt injection; agent security should abandon retaliation-by-detection and invest in compartmentalization, capability scoping, and bounded blast radius.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Stack Does Not Need Deterrence; It Needs Containment
article_ideas.video_title: The Man Who Predicted The Iran War: The Next 9/11 Will Target Your Bank Account! | Professor Jiang

article_ideas.angle: From reserve-currency enforcement to protocol semantics; compare best-effort versus enforced agent commitments.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent systems researchers and protocol designers
article_ideas.based_on: contract and a promise backed by US military hegemony
article_ideas.thesis: Agent coordination guarantees are only as strong as the enforcement substrate behind them; without verification, escrow, or accountability, inter-agent commitments are best-effort and should be documented and tested as such.
article_ideas.title: Multi-Agent Protocols Are Promises Without Police
article_ideas.video_title: The Man Who Predicted The Iran War: The Next 9/11 Will Target Your Bank Account! | Professor Jiang

article_ideas.angle: Scheduling and optimization for multi-provider agent systems
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Available subscription quota is treated as a first-class scheduling constraint
article_ideas.thesis: Agent orchestrators should treat provider quota as a first-class scheduling constraint and solve capability-constrained quota-aware placement; naive highest-quota routing trades quality for availability, so the right design is constrained optimization, not greedy quota maximization.
article_ideas.title: Stop Treating Model Quotas as an Ops Problem
article_ideas.video_title: High Throughput Agentic Engineering with ex-Meta L8 Principal

article_ideas.angle: Translate hiring-manager incentive misalignment into agent architecture: separate demand for task completion from authority to declare task completion.

article_ideas.angle: Connect larger sample sizes and stronger objectivity to concrete calibration-error experiments under distribution shift.

article_ideas.thesis: Pooled evaluators improve thresholds only when sample pooling and drift handling are explicit; otherwise centralization merely adds a queue and relocates the bias.
article_ideas.title: Centralization Is a Statistical Instrument, Not a Governance Fetish
article_ideas.video_title: Inside Bending Spoons: Finding Talent, Leveraging AI & Driving Operational Excellence | Luca Ferrari

article_ideas.angle: Frame shared runtime, context, and tool layer as an amortization bet with a coupling risk balance sheet.
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects and engineering leaders

article_ideas.thesis: Consolidating agent runtimes yields reuse and leverage, but creates correlated failure modes and a one-time migration cost per acquisition; value depends on where coupling starts destroying resilience.
article_ideas.title: The Migration Tax: What Platform Consolidation Actually Buys
article_ideas.video_title: Inside Bending Spoons: Finding Talent, Leveraging AI & Driving Operational Excellence | Luca Ferrari

article_ideas.angle: Set the build-vs-buy boundary for agent infrastructure against frontier model capability growth.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs and AI infrastructure leads
article_ideas.based_on: Where execution speed per head is the differentiator, own the workflow and runtime layer
article_ideas.thesis: Where execution speed per head is the differentiator, own the workflow and runtime layer rather than renting interchangeable parts; the maintenance tax is justified only while the fitted process and operating data remain durable against model progress.
article_ideas.title: Build the Harness, Rent the Model
article_ideas.video_title: Inside Bending Spoons: Finding Talent, Leveraging AI & Driving Operational Excellence | Luca Ferrari

article_ideas.angle: Reframe reported sandbox escapes as a security-engineering failure rather than a model misbehavior story, then map the required control plane.
article_ideas.audience: AI security engineers, evaluation platform teams, and safety infrastructure leads

article_ideas.thesis: Evaluation sandboxes for tool-using agents must be hardened like production systems; process or VM isolation is insufficient, and per-tool authorization plus network egress controls are required to prevent goal-directed escapes.

article_ideas.angle: Translate CI/CD release gating patterns into frontier model training pipelines and define the evidence required to unpause.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform leaders, MLOps engineers, and AI governance practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: We must pause training runs if safety cases are not met.
article_ideas.thesis: The only credible way to enforce a training pause is to make safety cases machine-checkable blocking artifacts inside the training pipeline, not advisory reports produced alongside capability work.
article_ideas.title: Safety Cases Should Block Training Runs Like Failing Tests Block Deploys
article_ideas.video_title: Altman: AI Beyond Human Control “Absolutely” Possible, Vows Safeguards | Titans and Disruptors

article_ideas.angle: Turn an operational definition into concrete benchmark design principles and release criteria.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers, benchmark designers, and product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: AGI means AI outperforming humans at economically viable work.
article_ideas.thesis: Defining AGI as outperforming humans at economically viable work makes the threshold falsifiable and testable, so benchmark builders should prioritize economic task substitution over abstract capability claims.
article_ideas.title: AGI Is Economic Substitution, Not a Vibe
article_ideas.video_title: Altman: AI Beyond Human Control “Absolutely” Possible, Vows Safeguards | Titans and Disruptors

article_ideas.angle: Argue for converting vague risk narratives into numeric budgets with defined block conditions and audit trails.
article_ideas.audience: AI governance, risk, and safety leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Taking a 10% chance of killing everyone by the end of the decade is unacceptable.
article_ideas.thesis: Quantified catastrophic risk can be operationalized like an SRE error budget, with explicit thresholds that gate training, deployment, and rollout decisions rather than remaining a philosophical concern.
article_ideas.title: P(Doom) Should Be an Error Budget for AI Releases
article_ideas.video_title: Altman: AI Beyond Human Control “Absolutely” Possible, Vows Safeguards | Titans and Disruptors

article_ideas.angle: Move review, versioning, and ownership of business logic to the semantic layer; treat confident-wrong answers as substrate defects.
article_ideas.audience: data platform leads and AI engineering teams
article_ideas.based_on: it multiplies its blast radius
article_ideas.thesis: Layering AI on unmastered data does not repair data-quality debt; it scales whatever definitional decisions the substrate encodes, so the gold/semantic layer must be treated as the AI correctness control surface.
article_ideas.title: AI Over an Ungoverned Data Estate Is an Error Amplifier, Not a Fix

article_ideas.angle: Use Managed Instance as the lowest-friction hop to preserve application contracts, and plan re-platforming separately.

article_ideas.based_on: Migration targets should be chosen for minimum rework, not maximum modernity
article_ideas.thesis: Under deadline, rank migration targets by rework cost and interface compatibility first; re-platforming is a second move, not the first.
article_ideas.title: The Boring Migration Target Wins: Compatibility Before Modernity
article_ideas.video_title: DATACON 2026: Building AI-Ready Microsoft Data Estates

article_ideas.angle: Treat EOL deadlines as forcing functions and front-load design lead time as a reliability control.
article_ideas.audience: CIOs, CTOs, and infrastructure planners
article_ideas.based_on: the schedule pressure, not the technology, is the causal defect
article_ideas.thesis: Schedule pressure, not technology, causes panic-driven architecture; deprecation dates should trigger front-loaded design and budget, not mobilization.
article_ideas.title: Your End-of-Support Date Is a Design Budget, Not a Start Signal
article_ideas.video_title: DATACON 2026: Building AI-Ready Microsoft Data Estates

article_ideas.angle: Add ownership and recency fields to tool catalogs and agent-accessible resource registries.
article_ideas.audience: data governance and platform engineering teams
article_ideas.based_on: Asset inventory must include ownership and last-usage dates, not just existence
article_ideas.thesis: Inventory only becomes a decision artifact when it carries owner, last-used, and dependency edges so staleness and orphanhood are machine-detectable.
article_ideas.title: An Inventory Without Owners and Last-Used Dates Is Just a List
article_ideas.video_title: DATACON 2026: Building AI-Ready Microsoft Data Estates

article_ideas.angle: Take the 27B-plus-external-tool configuration as evidence that the unit of competition has shifted from model to assembled system, then push on what that means for teams currently paying frontier-model margins for narrow workloads.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform architects choosing between proprietary APIs and open-weight fine-tuning
article_ideas.based_on: capability came from scaffolding plus reward design, not parameter scale
article_ideas.thesis: The Faraday result reframes the build-versus-buy decision: on narrow, deeply-specified tasks, investment in harness design and reward shaping dominates investment in base-model scale, and the right comparison is not model versus model but system versus system.
article_ideas.title: Capability Came From the Harness, Not the Parameters
article_ideas.video_title: What Building an AI Scientist Actually Requires Beyond Intelligence — Edward Hughes

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the rubric generator plus judge pattern is a reusable abstraction for every domain without unit tests, then detail the operational consequences: per-task artifact production, judge drift monitoring, and rubric-refresh cadence.
article_ideas.audience: Evaluation engineers and platform teams building agent training loops
article_ideas.based_on: A rubric generator produces task-specific criteria at runtime, and an LLM judge scores the trajectory against them.
article_ideas.thesis: When evaluation is generated per task rather than fixed in advance, rubric quality becomes a first-class engineering surface with its own latency, cost, and failure modes, and treating evaluation as static infrastructure guarantees that reward hacking is discovered late and expensively.
article_ideas.title: Your Evaluator Is a Pipeline Component Now
article_ideas.video_title: What Building an AI Scientist Actually Requires Beyond Intelligence — Edward Hughes

article_ideas.angle: Use AlphaGo's fixed rule set as the limiting case, then press on the practical question the argument avoids: how constraint-based search spaces are constructed and how one detects that an 'open-ended' loop has quietly become an objective maximizer.
article_ideas.audience: Researchers and architects working on curriculum generation and self-improvement loops
article_ideas.based_on: Optimization is structurally the wrong tool for creative discovery because it presupposes known objectives
article_ideas.thesis: Every system that claims open-endedness while training against a fixed objective is optimizing inside a known rule set, and constraints rather than objectives are the workable substitute for specifying search structure without specifying the target.
article_ideas.title: Optimization Cannot Discover the Problem It Is Optimizing
article_ideas.video_title: What Building an AI Scientist Actually Requires Beyond Intelligence — Edward Hughes

article_ideas.angle: Frame each hand-authored prompt, tool schema, and workflow edge as simultaneously guidance and generalization tax, and propose constraint-count regressions against held-out task performance as the diagnostic.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework authors and applied ML engineers shipping long-horizon agents
article_ideas.based_on: too much hardcoding limits generalization
article_ideas.thesis: Hardcoded scaffolding silently caps policy generalization, so harness rigidity should be treated as a measured design variable with an ablation budget rather than a fixed assumption baked in during the first demo.
article_ideas.title: The Harness Is the Ceiling
article_ideas.video_title: What Building an AI Scientist Actually Requires Beyond Intelligence — Edward Hughes

article_ideas.angle: Argues engineering leaders should reallocate budget from architecture R&D to data versioning, filtering, and dedup infrastructure, and warns that non-shareable data moats weaken independent reproducibility.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineering leaders, infrastructure teams, investors
article_ideas.based_on: Better data produces 12x improvement in compute efficiency
article_ideas.thesis: The reported 12x compute-efficiency gain from curated data versus 3.7x from architecture changes means proprietary curation pipelines, not model graphs, are the defensible asset and the primary lever for scaling.
article_ideas.title: Your Data Pipeline Is Your Moat: Why Curation Beats Architecture

article_ideas.angle: Frames memory-footprint-per-token as a first-class architecture metric and calls for quality benchmarks before celebrating cost wins.

article_ideas.thesis: Reducing per-token KV cache from hundreds of KB to 890 bytes is not just a memory trick; it changes what context windows and concurrency are economically viable, and HBM stops being the primary scaling constraint for cache-bound workloads.
article_ideas.title: Sub-KB KV Cache Is an Inference-Economics Inflection Point

article_ideas.thesis: Public and private safety resignations and warnings from frontier-lab staff are not virtue signaling; they are organizational signals that capability velocity is outrunning internal safety governance, and downstream integrators should treat deployment risk models as contested.
article_ideas.title: When Alignment Leads Resign, Treat It as a Leading Indicator
article_ideas.video_title: Three Lab Warnings in Five Days, Researcher Flags “Gambling with Our Lives,” and Labs Race

article_ideas.based_on: if it compiles it's ~correct
article_ideas.thesis: Strict type systems are a powerful but partial verification oracle; teams that treat compile-pass as semantic correctness will systematically miss requirement failures, so agent harnesses must add requirement-level checks.

article_ideas.angle: Reframe architecture as a governance and throughput lever.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers, architects, and CTOs.

article_ideas.thesis: The highest-leverage agent reliability investment is not prompt engineering but the architectural substrate: boundaries and invariants determine whether generated code composes or accumulates as slop.
article_ideas.title: Architecture Is the Agent Harness
article_ideas.video_title: Building ambitious software — Jonathan Kelley, Dioxus Labs & Cognition

article_ideas.angle: Cost-model argument for agent loop economics.
article_ideas.audience: Tooling builders and AI engineers.

article_ideas.thesis: Agent capability is bounded by attempts times iteration latency; sub-100ms hot-patching of native compiled code removes the historic either/or between strict verification and fast loops.

article_ideas.angle: Review economics and workflow redesign.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers and open-source maintainers.

article_ideas.thesis: As generation cost approaches zero, review becomes an intent-recovery process; scaling review requires pre-generation intent and interface contracts, not faster line-by-line reading.

article_ideas.angle: Invert the default additive instinct in tool and agent-role registries by requiring a deletion or explicit cost justification for every addition.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, platform architects, agent framework designers
article_ideas.based_on: Focus is defined as a subtractive discipline
article_ideas.thesis: Agent frameworks should govern capability surfaces with an explicit kill-list rather than an approval-list; coherence comes from removal, not addition, and the absence of kill criteria is the primary source of capability bloat.

article_ideas.angle: Compare latency, context coherence, and tool-protocol co-design potential in owned vs composed stacks.
article_ideas.audience: Technical leaders, agent platform builders, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: End-to-end ownership of both the platform substrate and the application layer is argued to be an advantage
article_ideas.thesis: When the hard problems live at layer boundaries, vertical integration of model, memory, tools, and runtime yields cross-layer optimizations that composed stacks cannot reach, at the cost of ecosystem breadth and lock-in accusations.

article_ideas.angle: Identify leading signals such as project churn, unretired commitments, and staffing mismatch against stated strategy.

article_ideas.based_on: The cited root cause of multi-year decline is managerial, not technical
article_ideas.thesis: The binding constraint on AI system quality is the decision layer above the engineering layer; instrumenting prioritization and staffing decisions can catch decline before it manifests in runtime metrics.
article_ideas.title: Lousy Engineering Management Is a Detectable Failure Mode

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the adoption statistic as an architecture requirement: treat process-change count as a first-class design constraint, with vertical integration engineering as the value-creating layer.
article_ideas.audience: AI product engineers and vertical SaaS founders
article_ideas.based_on: 76% of small businesses report using AI but only 14% have embedded it in core operations
article_ideas.thesis: Because the binding constraint is embedding AI into core operations rather than model capability, the winning engineering work is minimizing required process change — and teams that keep optimizing capability while ignoring integration cost will keep shipping pilots that never reach production.

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the defensibility claim only holds if knowledge capture and injection are treated as engineering infrastructure with elicitation, curation, and validation workflows — otherwise the moat is a claim without a mechanism.
article_ideas.audience: Technical founders and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: tacit operational knowledge is rare
article_ideas.thesis: If public training data commoditizes model capability, then the durable asset is proprietary tacit context and the mechanism that injects it — which means context engineering graduates from a prompt tactic to a versioned, maintainable subsystem deserving the same rigor as any other architectural component.
article_ideas.title: Your Moat Is the Context Store, Not the Model
article_ideas.video_title: The Biggest AI Opportunities Are Hiding in Boring Businesses

article_ideas.angle: Trace the causal chain from pricing decoupling to required instrumentation: outcome correctness, reproducibility, and attribution evidence that survives client dispute.
article_ideas.audience: AI service operators and agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: AI reduces the time required to complete tasks from days to minutes
article_ideas.thesis: When agents collapse task time from days to minutes, hour-based pricing stops tracking value, but the replacement only works if the system emits verifiable outcome signals — so pricing model choice is really an observability and evaluation requirement in disguise.

article_ideas.video_title: The Biggest AI Opportunities Are Hiding in Boring Businesses

article_ideas.angle: Turn the value-versus-adoption-friction tradeoff into an explicit selection heuristic, with the caveat that the same friction that protects you also lengthens your own sales cycle.
article_ideas.audience: Vertical AI founders and investors
article_ideas.based_on: The highest value problems are often the hardest to change and require deep domain expertise.
article_ideas.thesis: Because easy-to-enter niches attract competition and compress returns while specialized high-value problems stay expertise-gated and hard to change, defensibility comes from deliberately tolerating friction the market avoids — a positioning decision, not a technical one.

article_ideas.angle: Engineering management and infrastructure strategy
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, AI agent builders, DevOps teams
article_ideas.based_on: Verification, not code generation, is the binding constraint
article_ideas.thesis: The binding constraint in automated software engineering is verification capacity, not code generation; therefore, organizations should treat fault-injecting test harnesses and multiverse testing as core platform infrastructure, and shift success metrics from lines generated to verified changes per hour.
article_ideas.title: The Verifier is the Product: Why Coding Agents Must Be Measured in Verified Changes per Hour

article_ideas.angle: ML training strategy and cost optimization
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, AI researchers, technical leads

article_ideas.thesis: RL on long trajectories is information-theoretically wasteful, and the most cost-effective path to reasoning capability is SFT-seeded RL; teams should model training cost as tokens-per-reward-bit and make reward densification a first-class engineering deliverable.

article_ideas.angle: Research strategy and resource allocation
article_ideas.audience: ML strategists, research leads, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Empirically, data-side improvements dominate model/architecture improvements
article_ideas.thesis: Empirical attribution showing data improvements yield larger compute multipliers than architectural tweaks (12x vs 3.7x) implies that data pipelines deserve architecture-level investment, and over-indexing on architecture research is a strategic error at current scales.

article_ideas.angle: AI safety and research direction
article_ideas.audience: AI safety researchers, research strategists, policy analysts
article_ideas.based_on: The plausible ceiling on recursive self-improvement is not raw capability but generalization limits
article_ideas.thesis: The limiting factor for recursive self-improvement is not raw model capability but generalization limits in metalearning and continual learning, plus human advantages in objective specification and trade-off evaluation; therefore, self-improvement loops will remain evaluation-bound and require human-in-the-loop objective contracts.

article_ideas.angle: Trace the failure from the reflex ('add more data') to the measured outcome (85% accuracy with fairness degradation), then specify the gate: candidate pool, scoring function, top-K admission, and monitoring of the secondary metric.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform and data platform engineers, responsible-AI practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Naive data expansion — adding all available data or random data — can raise accuracy while degrading fairness
article_ideas.thesis: Because naive and random expansion can raise accuracy while degrading fairness, teams that instrument dataset size as their quality proxy are shipping silent metric regressions; every augmentation path — human-sourced or synthetic — needs a scored selection gate before data enters the training set.
article_ideas.title: Your Bias Fix Is a Selection Problem, Not a Volume Problem

article_ideas.angle: Argue from the structure of the failure (component parameter vs data quality in isolation) to the required abstraction, then sketch the artifact: nodes for profiles and components, edges to task utility, and interventions as edges of the graph.
article_ideas.audience: Data and ML platform architects, agent and orchestration builders
article_ideas.based_on: Pipeline failure diagnosis is modeled as a causal graph over data profiles and downstream utility rather than as per-stage inspection
article_ideas.thesis: Stage-local inspection cannot see cross-stage assumption violations, so any agent that proposes and ranks repairs needs an explicit graph over intermediate data profiles and downstream utility as a first-class artifact — logs and per-tool diagnostics are structurally insufficient, not merely incomplete.
article_ideas.title: Stop Debugging Stages, Start Debugging the Graph

article_ideas.angle: Cost-model the two-phase loop (proxy rank, then execute), then stress the assumption with novel shift types that past runs do not cover and quantify the hit-rate decay.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and reliability engineers responsible for ML/DS pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: Repair search is two-phase: cheap ranking from history and data profiles, then expensive execution
article_ideas.thesis: Automated repair over large configuration spaces only pencils out when a cheap ranking stage derived from retained execution history and data profiles precedes expensive execution, which forces a design decision most teams have not made: execution history is a durable asset, not disposable telemetry.
article_ideas.title: Rank Before You Run: Cheap Proxy Evaluation Is What Makes Self-Repair Affordable
article_ideas.video_title: 2026-09-09 CERIAS - Reasoning About Interventions in Data and Machine Learning Systems

article_ideas.angle: Use the 87%-to-39% F1 collapse as the case study, contrast parameter-only, structural-only, and mixed search spaces, and argue for minimality criteria that cover adding a stage as well as retuning one.
article_ideas.audience: Applied ML engineers, data quality and robustness researchers
article_ideas.based_on: the demonstrated fix was structural rather than parametric
article_ideas.thesis: Long-lived pipelines accumulate unstated input assumptions, and an intervention space restricted to parameters is provably unable to repair them — robustness work must include detection of assumption violations and synthesis of structural interventions, with minimality defined over a mixed edit space rather than a single one.
article_ideas.title: Assumption Debt: The Failure Class Parameter Tuning Cannot Reach
article_ideas.video_title: 2026-09-09 CERIAS - Reasoning About Interventions in Data and Machine Learning Systems

article_ideas.angle: Start from the PLA reroute incident as the concrete failure, then walk through the invisible hops (router, gateway, fallback, intermediate vendor) and show why client-side configuration and endpoint data-handling guarantees are structurally insufficient.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and infrastructure engineers building on third-party LLM APIs, plus AI governance and security architecture leads
article_ideas.based_on: every hop in the routing chain
article_ideas.thesis: Prompt confidentiality is a property of the routing chain, not of the named endpoint, so data-classification and redaction controls must be enforced at ingress to the chain and cross-provider routing must become an explicit, logged, policy-controlled decision.
article_ideas.title: The Model You Selected Is Not the Model That Saw Your Prompt
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Threat Report, AI's Effect on Cybercrime, and How 9/11 Changed Cybersecurity

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the sensationalized narrative (former employee's 10% extinction claim amplified credulously by mainstream news) with what the threat reporting actually shows: familiar groups using a new tool, with a human directing every step.
article_ideas.audience: CISOs, security architects, and security budget owners fending off modality-specific tooling pitches
article_ideas.based_on: Categorizing threat actors by motivation and origin rather than by the tools they use.
article_ideas.thesis: Adversaries are classified by motivation and origin, not by the tools they use; building defenses around an 'AI threat' abstraction pulls budget away from identity, MFA, and endpoint detection, which remain the primary entry points even as LLMs accelerate existing actor workflows.
article_ideas.title: There Is No AI Threat Category
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Threat Report, AI's Effect on Cybercrime, and How 9/11 Changed Cybersecurity

article_ideas.angle: Architectural teardown: show what a layered base-plus-pluggable-escalation design buys (domain policy changes without re-instrumenting the base, reuse of existing telemetry for new harm domains) versus what it costs in attribution ambiguity across a shared threat-group taxonomy.
article_ideas.audience: Trust and safety engineers and model-safety platform teams designing abuse-detection infrastructure
article_ideas.based_on: cybercrime and biological weapon development
article_ideas.thesis: Consolidating cybercrime and bio/CBRN abuse detection onto a single telemetry surface is viable only if generic misuse signals are separated from domain-specific escalation and reporting stages; a monolithic policy layer designed for one harm class will not survive contact with a second.
article_ideas.title: One Abuse Pipeline, Two Harm Domains
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Threat Report, AI's Effect on Cybercrime, and How 9/11 Changed Cybersecurity

article_ideas.angle: Historical lens: use the post-9/11 shift in vendor count and conference scale as the reference case, then apply the same reading to how today's AI-security category is being formed and funded.
article_ideas.audience: Procurement teams, security investors, and vendor-selection committees
article_ideas.based_on: a ~30-vendor niche into a major commercial sector
article_ideas.thesis: The funding shock that turned a roughly 30-vendor niche into a global commercial sector is a more durable predictor of vendor behavior than the vendor's own technical differentiation claims, so procurement and build-vs-buy decisions should be evaluated against capital-cycle dynamics.
article_ideas.title: Reading Security Vendors Through the Capital Cycle
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Threat Report, AI's Effect on Cybercrime, and How 9/11 Changed Cybersecurity

article_ideas.angle: Engineering-investment argument grounded in the AlphaGo recipe and its implied generalization to any domain with a fast simulator or checker.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform leads, and technical leads allocating R&D budget
article_ideas.based_on: constructing verifiable environments/verifiers
article_ideas.thesis: The transferable asset in agentic systems is the automatic verifier and its environment, not prompt text or hand-authored heuristics; teams that invest in checkable environments compound returns while prompt-centric stacks plateau, because learned evaluation replaces manual policy authoring.
article_ideas.title: Your Prompt Library Is Not the Moat - Your Verifier Is
article_ideas.video_title: Sir Demis Hassabis on Creativity and AI | Will AI Change How We Create? | Hannah Fry

article_ideas.angle: Distribution-strategy argument that treats the release decision, not the model, as the impact-shaping layer.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform and infrastructure teams, research organizations, and open-science program leads
article_ideas.based_on: publishing precomputed model outputs at scale can move a field faster than exposing the model itself
article_ideas.thesis: For high-volume, low-variance inference, bulk-publishing precomputed outputs as shared infrastructure drives adoption faster than gated model access, because it removes inference cost and ML expertise as barriers and relocates the bottleneck to downstream validation, provenance, and integration.
article_ideas.title: Ship the Outputs, Not the Model
article_ideas.video_title: Sir Demis Hassabis on Creativity and AI | Will AI Change How We Create? | Hannah Fry

article_ideas.angle: Governance-as-runtime-architecture argument, with outcome variance across identical models as the falsifiable claim.
article_ideas.audience: AI governance and safety practitioners, platform architects, and compliance engineering leads
article_ideas.based_on: Technology does not determine its own outcomes
article_ideas.thesis: Capability and outcome are decoupled, so evaluation, provenance, and decision rights should be designed as runtime components alongside the model rather than as post-hoc review gates; the wrapper is a first-class, testable engineering artifact.
article_ideas.title: The Wrapper Is the Product
article_ideas.video_title: Sir Demis Hassabis on Creativity and AI | Will AI Change How We Create? | Hannah Fry

article_ideas.angle: Operationalizing a vague amplification claim into an instrumentable product metric.
article_ideas.audience: Product teams building creative and generative tooling, and design-tooling engineers
article_ideas.based_on: measure and optimize iterations-per-hour and artifact continuity
article_ideas.thesis: The measurable content of AI-amplifies-creativity is reduced loop latency, so creative tooling should be optimized for iterations-per-hour and artifact continuity rather than peak per-call quality; the pairing of fast generation with rigorous verification is what makes the loop productive.
article_ideas.title: Tenfold Creativity Is a Latency Claim
article_ideas.video_title: Sir Demis Hassabis on Creativity and AI | Will AI Change How We Create? | Hannah Fry

article_ideas.angle: Reframe evaluation of agentic pipelines around perturbation handling, using last-minute event schedule changes as the canonical test case, and argue that most 'scaled' claims are unmeasured on this axis.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building high-fan-out generation pipelines; platform and design-ops leads evaluating automation ROI
article_ideas.based_on: how cheaply it absorbs exceptions
article_ideas.thesis: Volume generated on the happy path is a vanity metric for generative production systems; the real scaling property is time-to-incorporate-perturbation, and pipelines that hide their exception rate are repackaging manual labor as automation.
article_ideas.title: Your Agentic Pipeline's Only Honest Metric Is Exception Cost
article_ideas.video_title: One Designer + AI. Hundreds of Deliverables. — Vincent Wendy, AI Engineer

article_ideas.angle: Use the raster-then-vectorize workaround as the worked example and generalize it to a routing rule for any multi-tool agent system with a format-specific weak spot.
article_ideas.audience: Agent/tooling engineers, design technologists, prompt-engineering practitioners tired of format whack-a-mole
article_ideas.based_on: vectorize it in Figma to bypass native SVG generation flaws
article_ideas.thesis: Capability-boundary routing — generating in a modality the model handles well and converting with deterministic tooling — beats prompt iteration on output formats the model cannot reliably produce, and the converter is the testable component.
article_ideas.title: Stop Asking the Model for the Format It's Bad At
article_ideas.video_title: One Designer + AI. Hundreds of Deliverables. — Vincent Wendy, AI Engineer

article_ideas.angle: Argue that prompt-level constraint specification and programmatic artifact linting are different guarantees, and that only the latter is auditable at hundreds of outputs.
article_ideas.audience: Design systems engineers, brand/design ops leaders, AI-platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: LLMs left unconstrained will introduce random font sizes
article_ideas.thesis: When an agent writes the design file, a design system documented as guidance is worthless; it must be machine-enforceable constraint that is validated on rendered output, because a single unconstrained generation step contaminates every derivative artifact.
article_ideas.title: Design Systems Must Become Executable Contracts Once Agents Are the Primary Authors
article_ideas.video_title: One Designer + AI. Hundreds of Deliverables. — Vincent Wendy, AI Engineer

article_ideas.angle: Interrogate the sponsor-logo and headshot validation claims as a methodology problem: sample size, defect taxonomy, occlusion and near-duplicate cases, and the escalation path that detects verifier failure.
article_ideas.audience: QA/reliability engineers, ML evaluation researchers, production owners of model-based review gates
article_ideas.based_on: 100% accuracy for the logo check
article_ideas.thesis: Self-reported near-perfect model validation accuracy on mass-produced artifacts is an unverified load-bearing assumption; without an adversarial defect benchmark, verifier failure ships silently at exactly the volume where it is least detectable.
article_ideas.title: The 100% Validation Claim Is Where Agentic Production Will Break
article_ideas.video_title: One Designer + AI. Hundreds of Deliverables. — Vincent Wendy, AI Engineer

article_ideas.angle: Argue for replaceable wrapper seams and capability-jump instrumentation as the durable engineering assets, using the rebuild-from-scratch event as the failure case.
article_ideas.audience: AI product engineering leaders and platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: model capability improvements accrue value automatically
article_ideas.thesis: At foundation-model companies, thin wrappers over scaling laws are rational only if the architecture underneath them is explicitly disposable at model-generation boundaries; otherwise capability jumps convert yesterday's product advantage into tomorrow's rebuild cost.
article_ideas.title: The Scaling-Law Product Is Disposable by Design
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Head of Design on AGI-Maximalist Product Design | Joel Lewenstein

article_ideas.angle: Reconcile the claim that internal traction is the best viability signal with the risk of internal digital divides; propose measuring false-positive rate of the internal-readiness gate.
article_ideas.audience: Product, eval, and launch leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Internal traction is the best signal of product viability
article_ideas.thesis: Internal dogfooding is a high-fidelity eval harness, but it systematically overpredicts external success when internal users have higher AI fluency and shared context, so release gates must be stratified and fluency-adjusted.
article_ideas.title: Internal Traction Is Not External Readiness
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Head of Design on AGI-Maximalist Product Design | Joel Lewenstein

article_ideas.angle: Use the Claude Artifacts UI shift as evidence that separating the meta-conversation from the artifact is an architectural boundary with runtime consequences.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform and developer-tool engineers
article_ideas.based_on: The output artifact and the meta-conversation are separate architectural surfaces
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic systems that generate durable objects should model those objects as first-class versioned state with their own lifecycle and render target, because append-only transcripts cap downstream tooling and force generated artifacts into text blobs.
article_ideas.title: Artifacts Are State, Not Messages
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Head of Design on AGI-Maximalist Product Design | Joel Lewenstein

article_ideas.angle: Challenge the growth-hacking default of maximum shipping velocity with the user-fatigue thought experiment and propose fatigue metrics.
article_ideas.audience: Product designers and growth teams in AI
article_ideas.based_on: Shipping velocity without deliberate curation produces user fatigue
article_ideas.thesis: When the model supplies marginal capability, product growth stops being feature-throughput-limited and becomes attention-and-trust-limited, making release pacing, editorial restraint, and feature removal measurable first-class levers.
article_ideas.title: Curate or Fatigue: The Binding Constraint When Features Are Cheap
article_ideas.video_title: Anthropic's Head of Design on AGI-Maximalist Product Design | Joel Lewenstein

article_ideas.angle: Contrarian eval-engineering argument grounded in AUC/cost tradeoff.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, eval teams, platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Slop probes separate designer-approved from designer-rejected sites at AUC 0.74
article_ideas.thesis: For subjective quality gates like design slop, lightweight pattern probes are a better default evaluator than LLM-as-judge because they are cheaper, faster, and—at least in the reported design case—more discriminative, so teams should adopt probe-first pipelines and reserve LLM judges for edge cases.
article_ideas.title: Your Aesthetic Judge Should Be a Baby Classifier (Not a Prompt)
article_ideas.video_title: Training Taste — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs

article_ideas.angle: Architecture argument for structured context over long system prompts.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers, product engineers, design systems teams
article_ideas.based_on: Brand API extracts structured brand components from a URL
article_ideas.thesis: Brand adherence should not be a prose instruction; it should be an inspectable runtime API that extracts structured brand components and lets agents score their own outputs, converting taste from implicit prompt hint to verifiable interface.
article_ideas.title: Stop Prompting for Brand, Ship a Brand API
article_ideas.video_title: Training Taste — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs

article_ideas.angle: Framework article with concrete failure-axis instrumentation.
article_ideas.audience: Design engineers, AI product leads, quality platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: decomposed into four measurable pillars
article_ideas.thesis: Subjective quality problems are tractable once decomposed into repetition, fit, intent, and judgment, each with a distinct mechanism; teams should instrument these axes separately instead of asking one model 'is this good?'
article_ideas.title: The Four Pillars of Taste Engineering
article_ideas.video_title: Training Taste — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs

article_ideas.angle: Strategic/architectural argument about value migration to verification.
article_ideas.audience: Founders, CTOs, AI infrastructure investors
article_ideas.based_on: cost of generation is going to zero
article_ideas.thesis: As generation cost approaches zero, the scarce resource is judgment and verification; the strategic investment shifts from better generators to runtime constraint layers, probes, and brand APIs that gate outputs.
article_ideas.title: When Generation Is Free, Build the Gatehouse
article_ideas.video_title: Training Taste — Thais Castello Branco, Taste Labs

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the vocabulary layer—not the model—is the stable abstraction boundary teams should invest in, test, and share.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, design technologists, developer-tooling teams
article_ideas.based_on: Design intent can be encoded as a constrained vocabulary of adjectives and verbs
article_ideas.thesis: Open prompts and pixel tools are both inadequate; the durable control plane for AI-assisted design is a constrained, versioned lexicon of adjectives and verbs that compiles to design-system operations.
article_ideas.title: The Adjective Is the Interface: Why Generative Design Needs a Versioned Vocabulary
article_ideas.video_title: Design at the Speed of Adjectives — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek, Inc.

article_ideas.angle: Reframe 'AI slop' from a model-quality complaint into an agent-design pattern: build decision-forcing loops.
article_ideas.audience: Agent designers, AI product engineers, technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: One-shot design generation is claimed to be structurally unviable
article_ideas.thesis: One-shot generation produces generic output not because models lack capability but because the prompt delegates every decision; quality rises when the workflow forces explicit decision points and multi-shot refinement.
article_ideas.title: One-Shot Design Is a Decision-Allocation Failure
article_ideas.video_title: Design at the Speed of Adjectives — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek, Inc.

article_ideas.angle: Treat identical SaaS aesthetics and purple gradients as measurable production debt, not just aesthetic taste.
article_ideas.audience: Design leaders, AI platform teams, brand strategists
article_ideas.based_on: Taste is characterized as cultural, contextual, and scarce
article_ideas.thesis: Shared base models exert convergence pressure toward generic aesthetics; differentiation must come from unique context, constraints, or post-training, and output diversity should be measured as a quality metric.
article_ideas.title: Taste Is Scarce: Homogenization as a Production Hazard
article_ideas.video_title: Design at the Speed of Adjectives — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek, Inc.

article_ideas.angle: Show how shell-like domain verbs become the interface to generative agents, with CI and semantic versioning.
article_ideas.audience: Developer-tooling teams, agent platform engineers, design-system maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: Reusable, named, community-tested commands
article_ideas.thesis: Community-tested named commands should be modeled as a versioned, testable operation library rather than free-text prompts, enabling regression testing and cross-team reuse of agent behavior.
article_ideas.title: Named Ops Beat Vague Prompts: Design Commands as a Versioned DSL
article_ideas.video_title: Design at the Speed of Adjectives — Paul Bakaus, Renaissance Geek, Inc.

article_ideas.angle: Use Amdahl's law and the 8x merge-volume observation to argue that agent platforms must budget and instrument the verifier as a first-class pipeline component.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: As execution gets cheap, the bottleneck shifts to verification.
article_ideas.thesis: Once generation is cheap, end-to-end throughput is capped by the serialized human verification stage, so engineering effort should shift from generator speed to verifier throughput and review-assist tooling.
article_ideas.title: The Verification Ceiling: Why Faster Agents Don't Ship Faster Software
article_ideas.video_title: Mousepower: agents that can’t be measured, can’t be managed. — Maximillian Piras, Yutori

article_ideas.angle: Trace how output metrics become organizational incentives, then propose run-level outcome attribution as the instrumentation schema change that breaks the cycle.
article_ideas.audience: AI product managers and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Tokens are an output, not an outcome.
