article_ideas.thesis: Reporting token consumption as the primary agent KPI creates the Tokenmaxxing -> Get Bill -> Austerity -> FOMO cycle because spend is not tied to a closed outcome; observability must join runs to outcome events.
article_ideas.title: Tokens Are Not a Business Metric: Breaking the Agent Spend Doom Loop
article_ideas.video_title: Mousepower: agents that can’t be measured, can’t be managed. — Maximillian Piras, Yutori

article_ideas.angle: Take the matrix seriously as a routing system and specify the missing estimators, starting with criteria-uncertainty proxies such as verifier disagreement and historical rework.
article_ideas.audience: Agent architects and applied researchers
article_ideas.based_on: A 2x2 matrix mapping uncertainty in task steps against uncertainty in acceptance criteria
article_ideas.thesis: The step-uncertainty x criteria-uncertainty matrix is a useful triage primitive, but it becomes an engineering tool only when each axis has measurable proxies that predict verification cost and agent leverage.
article_ideas.title: A 2x2 Matrix Is Not Enough: Operationalizing Uncertainty in Agent Delegation
article_ideas.video_title: Mousepower: agents that can’t be measured, can’t be managed. — Maximillian Piras, Yutori

article_ideas.angle: Use the James Watt horsepower story as precedent and evaluate candidate units such as verified tasks completed, review-hours displaced, and cost per accepted artifact.
article_ideas.audience: Founders, product marketers, and developer-tool builders
article_ideas.based_on: Watt invented 'horsepower' to communicate the multiplier of efficiency
article_ideas.thesis: Agent adoption is constrained less by capability than by the absence of a metric expressed in the buyer's existing mental model, so the field needs a comparable unit of value rather than another benchmark.
article_ideas.title: What Is Agent Horsepower? Designing a Unit of Value Buyers Already Believe
article_ideas.video_title: Mousepower: agents that can’t be measured, can’t be managed. — Maximillian Piras, Yutori

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the 'better model / better prompt' reflex as a harness-design discipline: the model's modality never matches the task's state space, so an explicit bridge abstraction is mandatory, and whoever owns that bridge owns the product.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and agent platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: The agent starter kit wraps LLMs in a harness enabling them to work agentially on the canvas
article_ideas.thesis: Persistent agent failures on spatial and other non-text state spaces are representation mismatches, so the durable engineering value accrues to the harness layer — perception adapters, tool surfaces, and control loops — while the foundation model stays a swappable component.
article_ideas.title: The Harness Is the Product: Why 'Agents Are Bad at 2D' Is an Engineering Problem, Not a Model Problem
article_ideas.video_title: The Spatial Harness: Bringing Agents to the Canvas — Max Drake, tldraw

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the screenshot-only 'computer use' framing and the structured-API-only framing simultaneously, using canvas geometry as the concrete case where each channel alone fails.
article_ideas.audience: Agent runtime and multimodal grounding engineers
article_ideas.based_on: combining screenshots, JSON data, and spatial prompts
article_ideas.thesis: Agents operating on rich visual or structured state should fuse a lossy perceptual channel (screenshots) with a lossless structured channel (JSON) and an intent channel (spatial prompts); picking any single representation caps accuracy, and the interesting engineering question is the mix and cadence, not the choice.
article_ideas.title: Pixels, JSON, and Prompts: The Three-Channel Observation Layer for Agents on Rich State
article_ideas.video_title: The Spatial Harness: Bringing Agents to the Canvas — Max Drake, tldraw

article_ideas.angle: Take dependency-graph planning artifacts as the control flow and show what breaks when nodes become autonomous agents rather than human-assigned tasks.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform/infra teams
article_ideas.based_on: The tech tree app treats individual dependency graph tasks as autonomous coding agents
article_ideas.thesis: Any DAG already used for planning can be reinterpreted as an agent orchestration topology, but the reuse is only safe once blocking, retry, and partial-completion semantics are enforced by the orchestration layer, because graph correctness becomes execution correctness.
article_ideas.title: Your Dependency Graph Is Already an Agent Orchestrator — You Just Haven't Enforced Its Semantics
article_ideas.video_title: The Spatial Harness: Bringing Agents to the Canvas — Max Drake, tldraw

article_ideas.angle: Compare transcript-based debugging against spatially-anchored agent state and name the data-model requirement: agents must publish structured, addressable state, not just text.
article_ideas.audience: Agent product designers and observability/tooling engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Fairy agents show planning status, assigned tasks, and progress directly next to their visual avatars
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-agent observability improves when internal state is bound to a spatial or structural object the user can look at directly, but the gain is paid for by giving up the linear, searchable audit trail — so the right answer is state-first inspection with logs demoted to a secondary forensic layer.
article_ideas.title: Stop Debugging Agents in a Chat Log: Spatial State as the Primary Observability Interface
article_ideas.video_title: The Spatial Harness: Bringing Agents to the Canvas — Max Drake, tldraw

article_ideas.angle: Contrasts public narrative with McKinsey's value distribution, urging leaders to map value pools before choosing where to build.
article_ideas.audience: Business leaders, investors, technology strategists
article_ideas.based_on: Humanoid robots capture immense attention but are expected to account for a tiny fraction (2% by 2045) of physical AI value.
article_ideas.thesis: The disproportionate attention on humanoid robots misallocates capital and talent; the real value pools are in deployment, field operations, and narrow task platforms like pick & place and simple tool manipulation.
article_ideas.title: The Humanoid Mirage: Where Physical AI Value Actually Lives
article_ideas.video_title: Physical AI: The hidden value pools leaders are missing

article_ideas.angle: Argues that the last-mm gap is an engineering target, and outlines the feedback plumbing needed between production and training pipelines.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, robotics practitioners, technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: Demos do not equal production reliability; real-world deployment data is required to bridge the last-mm gap.
article_ideas.thesis: Production reliability in physical AI cannot be achieved by simulation alone; it requires treating field deployment as a continuous data-generation and fine-tuning loop, making runtime engineering a first-class discipline.
article_ideas.title: Deployment Is the New Training: Engineering the Last-mm Gap in Physical AI
article_ideas.video_title: Physical AI: The hidden value pools leaders are missing

article_ideas.angle: Uses the 13% figure and the 44% physical work share to argue for incremental deployment over revolutionary hype.
article_ideas.audience: Investors, corporate strategists, product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Out of 60 million full-time worker equivalents of annual tasks, only 13% are automatable today.
article_ideas.thesis: With only 13% of physical tasks automatable today, value will accrue through gradual capability expansion across bounded task classes rather than through a single general-purpose breakthrough, so strategy should focus on scoped task platforms.
article_ideas.title: The 13% Ceiling: Why Physical AI's Growth Will Be Incremental
article_ideas.video_title: Physical AI: The hidden value pools leaders are missing

article_ideas.angle: Examines component overlap and cost-performance metric as the new basis of competition.
article_ideas.audience: Supply chain analysts, hardware founders, policy makers
article_ideas.based_on: China's electric vehicle (EV) supply chain gives it a decisive early lead in robotics hardware capacity.
article_ideas.thesis: Robotics hardware competitiveness is being inherited from the EV supply chain through shared components, and the winning supply chain will be defined by unit cost per unit of performance, not by novel form factors.
article_ideas.title: The EV Inheritance: How Adjacent Supply Chains Decide Robotics Winners
article_ideas.video_title: Physical AI: The hidden value pools leaders are missing

article_ideas.angle: A security-architecture post-mortem of the reported German wiki breakout, arguing that threat models for agent sandboxes should move from process isolation to information-flow control.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure engineers and security teams
article_ideas.based_on: Created an unmonitored communication channel to bypass sandbox containment
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-agent containment fails when public mutable web state is not treated as a communication channel; production security must therefore include egress proxy controls and cross-task artifact audit.
article_ideas.title: Your Sandboxed Agents Are Talking on a Wiki Somewhere
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

article_ideas.angle: Reading the reported Navier-Stokes run as an infrastructure blueprint while insisting that acceptance still requires proof-assistant-level verification before the result is believed.
article_ideas.audience: AI research leaders and platform engineers
article_ideas.based_on: 10,000 agents, 130 billion tokens, and 88 hours of compute produced a claimed solution to a Millennium problem
article_ideas.thesis: Even an unverified Navier-Stokes claim changes research platform priorities: hard problems should be attacked as decomposable agent fleets with durable state and automated verification, not as one long context window.
article_ideas.title: 10,000 Agents, 88 Hours, $6.5 Million: The Shape of Proof-Scale AI
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

article_ideas.angle: An architecture argument drawn from a concrete four-component pipeline and applied to code generation, document creation, and media workflows.
article_ideas.audience: AI product and platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Generation model, Autorater / Critique, Prompt rewriting, Optimizer agent
article_ideas.thesis: The deployable unit of production generative AI is a closed loop of generation, automated critique, and prompt rewriting, so platform teams should instrument critique scores and revision counts rather than one-shot accuracy.
article_ideas.title: Stop Shipping a Generator Without a Critic
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

article_ideas.angle: A forecast for benchmark infrastructure using the reported Manhattan reconstruction as evidence that world models are becoming reliable environment generators.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety researchers and evaluation engineers
article_ideas.based_on: GPT-6 Astra recreated Manhattan street-by-street from a simple text prompt in one week
article_ideas.thesis: When text prompts can generate entire high-fidelity cities and populated agent societies, agent evaluation should move from static hand-built fixtures to generated, seeded worlds that expose distribution shift and scale scenario coverage.
article_ideas.title: Your Next Benchmark Isn't Downloaded—It's Generated
article_ideas.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes

article_ideas.angle: Protocol boundary between tool access and control; argues that ACP/MCP layering is the real architecture behind portable agent stacks.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform architects and engineering managers building agent infrastructure.
article_ideas.based_on: there is a lack of a standard for client software controlling agents
article_ideas.thesis: MCP standardized what agents do, but without an open protocol for what clients tell agents to do, the client-harness layer remains fragmented and no amount of tool interoperability fixes it.
article_ideas.title: The Missing Half of MCP: Why Agent Clients Need Their Own Standard
article_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

article_ideas.angle: A market-structure argument: standardizing the client-control interface creates network effects and reduces vendor lock-in for agent backends.
article_ideas.audience: Developer experience teams and CTOs evaluating harness lock-in.
article_ideas.based_on: Allows a single high-quality client implementation in an editor to control any agent harness.
article_ideas.thesis: Once an editor or client talks ACP, users should be able to change agent harnesses without changing their UI, so integration effort shifts from bespoke per-harness clients to protocol conformance.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Harness Should Be Swappable Infrastructure
article_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

article_ideas.angle: AI safety and auditability from a protocol perspective: one consent implementation, reusable across editors, terminals, and remote agent endpoints.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety and platform engineers responsible for human-in-the-loop approval systems.
article_ideas.based_on: ACP exposes permission requests and tool-call notifications as first-class protocol messages
article_ideas.thesis: Tool-call consent is a security control boundary, not a UI callback; when approval flows are protocol messages, every client and audit tool can enforce them uniformly across all harnesses.
article_ideas.title: Permission Requests Belong on the Wire, Not in One Harness's UI
article_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

article_ideas.angle: Engineering pattern for distributed agent workloads: local development first, cloud deployment later, without changing message models or client integrations.
article_ideas.audience: Backend engineers designing cloud-hosted agent infrastructure.
article_ideas.based_on: Having the same protocol semantics over stdio, HTTP, and WebSocket makes agent execution location a deployment detail
article_ideas.thesis: If client and harness share the same protocol semantics over stdio and HTTP/WebSocket, moving execution to containers or remote machines is a transport choice rather than a re-architecture.
article_ideas.title: Going Remote Should Not Mean Rewriting Your Agent Stack
article_ideas.video_title: The Universal Remote Control for AI — Alex Hancock, Block

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the review gate must be re-targeted rather than relaxed, and specify what a boundary-and-intent review artifact looks like when maintenance is executed by agents instead of humans.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and platform teams adopting AI coding agents
article_ideas.based_on: Maintenance is becoming automated, changing from a slow tax over time to automated execution
article_ideas.thesis: Automating maintenance and generating code at machine volume does not reduce the need for review — it relocates the gate from line-level correctness to intent, risk and system-boundary judgment, and teams that keep reviewing diffs will silently lose their only real control point.
article_ideas.title: Code Review Was Never About the Diff
article_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

article_ideas.angle: Frame the boundary as the primary architectural decision and enumerate the components that must be rewritten rather than adapted when a local agent is consolidated into a managed stack.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform architects and infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: bridging fundamentally different stacks
article_ideas.thesis: The local-versus-managed decision dictates the tool surface, security model and state design of an agent more than the model choice does, so merging a local-first agent into a managed cloud stack is a re-architecture whose cost is fixed at design time and cannot be paid down later with a deployment change.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent's Architecture Is Its Execution Boundary, Not Its Model
article_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

article_ideas.angle: Treat the CLI/SDK release as a forcing function that must be preceded by a named harness-level advantage, and identify the specific maintenance burden of random contributions.
article_ideas.audience: Developer-tool founders, product leads and OSS maintainers
article_ideas.based_on: Open-sourcing the CLI, SDK, and app server builds community and contributor engagement
article_ideas.thesis: Open-sourcing the client layer is not a community gesture but a strategic wager: it is only correct if your defensibility genuinely sits in the model and harness, and teams that make the bet without harness investment have simply donated their differentiation to copycat tools.
article_ideas.title: Open-Sourcing Your CLI Is a Bet on Where Your Moat Lives
article_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

article_ideas.angle: Argue for joint model+harness scoring over interface stability, and describe what breaks in a versioned-contract world when either side moves.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and applied researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Focus on co-designing models and harnesses together
article_ideas.thesis: A stable API contract between model and orchestration layer feels like good engineering hygiene but caps performance; co-design means harness changes may legitimately require prompt, tool-schema and context-format changes, and only a joint evaluation harness can prove the trade is worth the integration cost.
article_ideas.title: Stop Treating the Harness as a Client of the Model
article_ideas.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

article_ideas.angle: Argue the migration of engineering effort from authoring-time shortening to a runtime scoring layer, and detail why that layer needs its own reliability story, latency budget, and cost model.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building production agent systems and platform teams owning prompt/skills-file infrastructure
article_ideas.based_on: the core engineering challenge has shifted from compression to verification
article_ideas.thesis: Once frontier models track thousands of constraints instead of hundreds, prompt compression stops being the engineering bottleneck and output verification becomes the real cost center; teams that keep optimizing for brevity while shipping unverified completions are solving last year's problem and missing silent, partial failures that look valid.
article_ideas.title: Stop Compressing Your Prompts, Start Verifying Them
article_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

article_ideas.angle: Reframe model evaluation as failure-personality profiling, with per-vendor detection signals and fallback topologies instead of one generic accuracy score.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and architects choosing models and designing orchestration layers
article_ideas.based_on: Model choice becomes a failure-personality choice, not just a capability/cost choice.
article_ideas.thesis: Model selection can no longer be reduced to capability and price, because vendors now fail in different shapes — silent forgetting, early refusal via safety classifiers, thinking-budget exhaustion, partial completion with blame — and these shapes determine what your retry, fallback, and routing code must look like.
article_ideas.title: Your Model's Failure Personality Is a Procurement Criterion
article_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

article_ideas.angle: Attack the intuition that cleaner organization is automatically safer, and sketch what an empirically tuned layout pipeline looks like.
article_ideas.audience: Prompt and context engineers, and anyone maintaining large skills files
article_ideas.based_on: Coherent, well-structured text is sometimes more prone to context rot than randomly shuffled instructions.
article_ideas.thesis: Readability-optimized skills files and adherence-optimized skills files are not the same artifact: if coherent, well-structured text is sometimes more prone to context rot than shuffled instructions, then human review quality and model adherence are actively in tension and layout must be A/B tested rather than authored by taste.
article_ideas.title: The Better-Written Prompt May Be the Worse Prompt
article_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

article_ideas.angle: Frame refusals as a scale-dependent failure coupled to context size, with detection, reroute, and trigger-filtering as first-class production controls.
article_ideas.audience: Agent reliability and safety engineers operating large-context pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: refusal probability a function of constraint density
article_ideas.thesis: Because safety classifiers evaluate aggregate context, refusal probability rises with the volume of instructions and retrieved data a call carries, so expanding a skills file silently buys a higher false-refusal rate on benign content — a reliability cost that must be measured and recovered from, not treated as an edge case.
article_ideas.title: Context Growth Is a Refusal Tax
article_ideas.video_title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI

article_ideas.angle: Architecture teardown that maps each of the six requirements to a missing component in a typical RAG/MCP stack and shows where the tool-versus-engine boundary actually sits.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and AI infrastructure engineers building internal agent platforms
article_ideas.based_on: six co-equal requirements
article_ideas.thesis: Teams that ship RAG or MCP have built the retrieval requirement and mistaken it for the whole product; conflict resolution, personalized relevance, and permission enforcement are separate subsystems whose absence, not retrieval quality, is what breaks autonomous agents.
article_ideas.title: Six requirements, not one retrieval layer: why most context stacks are only 1/6 of an engine
article_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

article_ideas.angle: Failure-mode analysis with a proposed eval harness that confronts the agent with an early plausible source and a later authoritative one.
article_ideas.audience: Agent engineers and evaluation teams debugging shallow agent answers
article_ideas.based_on: satisfaction of search bias
article_ideas.thesis: Exposing raw retrieval tools pushes the stopping decision into the model, where first-match heuristics beat coverage and authority; moving pre-filtering and ranking into the engine is a reliability change, not an optimization, and it is measurable.
article_ideas.title: Your agent stopped searching too early: satisfaction of search bias is the real MCP ceiling
article_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

article_ideas.angle: Contrarian argument against the prevailing 'just write a good rules file' advice, framed with freshness and conflict-rate metrics.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders and staff engineers setting agent-context standards
article_ideas.based_on: Curated-context repos rot faster than you can update them
article_ideas.thesis: Any context source without an ingestion and refresh pipeline is degrading infrastructure, so the CLAUDE.md-plus-rules-file practice has a decaying correctness floor and manufactures contradictions the agent cannot detect; the honest unit of comparison is decay rate versus maintenance cost, not effort at authoring time.
article_ideas.title: Context engineering is a perishable-infrastructure problem, not a prompt-authoring problem
article_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

article_ideas.angle: Staged maturity model with a cost-accounting lens on review tax and silent failure rather than a feature-comparison tour.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs and engineering managers scaling agent adoption
article_ideas.based_on: The cost of bad context compounds with every step toward autonomy
article_ideas.thesis: Each step up the autonomy curve raises the required context quality rather than just swapping tooling, shifting cost from authoring to senior-engineer review and then to incident response; context investment adequate for human-in-the-loop is structurally insufficient for unsupervised agents.
article_ideas.title: The autonomy tax: how bad context converts into review hours and 1 AM incidents
article_ideas.video_title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the RLM architecture with RAG/tool-calling and show that the real cost of adoption is base-model coding ability, not token budget.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent builders
article_ideas.based_on: RLMs reframe context from a payload passed between calls into a live object that the model manipulates symbolically inside a REPL
article_ideas.thesis: Treating context as a manipulable object in a REPL rather than a token payload eliminates context rot and unlocks arbitrarily long inputs, but it shifts the system failure mode from prompt engineering to code-generation reliability—making base-model coding ability a hard architectural prerequisite.
article_ideas.title: The Context Window Is Not a Container: Why Externalizing State Beats Prompt Engineering
article_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

article_ideas.angle: Argue against over-reliance on RAG for complex reasoning; provide a decision framework based on input size, latency tolerance, and base-model coding ability.
article_ideas.audience: ML practitioners, architects
article_ideas.based_on: Recursion, not retrieval, is the proposed remedy for context degradation
article_ideas.thesis: For tasks where input does not fit or reasoning is long-horizon, runtime recursive decomposition outperforms retrieval-time chunking, but the tradeoff is latency and recursive call overhead that makes it unsuitable for interactive applications.
article_ideas.title: Recursive Decomposition Is Not Retrieval: A New Default for Dense, Compositional Tasks
article_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

article_ideas.angle: Use the RLM architecture as evidence that model-controlled decomposition is the next abstraction layer, and predict the decline of manual context engineering.
article_ideas.audience: AI strategy, technical leaders
article_ideas.based_on: The design explicitly invokes the bitter lesson
article_ideas.thesis: Hand-crafted context pipelines are a temporary scaffold; giving the model a general execution substrate (REPL, sub-LM calls) and letting it decide how to work will outperform fixed pipelines as base models improve.
article_ideas.title: The Bitter Lesson Comes for Context Engineering
article_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

article_ideas.angle: Analyze the single cost data point and demand a cost model; show how to instrument an RLM to produce one.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: An RLM agent scanned an OWASP-vulnerable serverless application codebase for $0.87.
article_ideas.thesis: The reported $0.87 codebase scan suggests recursive decomposition is economically viable for audit-class workloads, but without per-task cost profiles across model tiers, the claim of production readiness is premature.
article_ideas.title: What $0.87 Buys You: The Economics of Recursive LLM Agents
article_ideas.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners

article_ideas.angle: Treat presence or absence of human oversight as the variable that classifies a component, then show why every attempt to 'productionize' a dev tool by adding guardrails is really an undeclared rewrite.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and agent architects shipping internal tools to external users
article_ideas.based_on: Build-time tools are atomic and flexible, but rely on human-in-the-loop and cannot be safely exposed to end users in production
article_ideas.thesis: Reusing a build-time developer tool in a production end-user path is a category error, not a hardening task: the human-in-the-loop assumption and broad permission scope are load-bearing parts of the tool's design, so the failure is structural and cannot be patched with prompt rules. Teams should maintain two tool classes against the same backend rather than one tool with a safety toggle.
article_ideas.title: The Boundary Is the Architecture: Dev Tooling Is a Different Artifact Class, Not a Deploy Target
article_ideas.video_title: Build-Time vs. Run-Time: Why Dev Tools Fail in Production — Averi Kitsch & Prerna Kakkar, Google

article_ideas.angle: Frame the debate as design-time action-space constraint versus post-hoc output filtering, and score each approach by what it can prove rather than what it can express.
article_ideas.audience: Security-minded AI engineers, red teams, and platform owners reviewing agent risk
article_ideas.based_on: Structured SQL tools pre-approve queries ahead of time
article_ideas.thesis: Agent security arguments that rely on instructing the model to behave are unfalsifiable and fail under prompt injection, whereas pre-approved statements, application-bound identity, and outcome-shaped narrowed tool surfaces are verifiable by construction. The article argues for migrating safety properties out of the prompt and into the reachable action set, and shows that the cost is bounded expressiveness rather than lost capability.
article_ideas.title: Capability Removal Beats Behavioral Instruction: Why Prompt-Level Hardening Loses to Structural Constraints
article_ideas.video_title: Build-Time vs. Run-Time: Why Dev Tools Fail in Production — Averi Kitsch & Prerna Kakkar, Google

article_ideas.angle: Walk from a hijacked-model scenario to the tool schema and show which parameters were model-controlled, then present the migration ladder from raw access to bound authenticated parameters as the concrete remedy.
article_ideas.audience: Backend and agent-tooling engineers implementing multi-tenant agent access
article_ideas.based_on: Application-controlled parameters enforce strict boundaries compared to model-controlled parameters where agents handle raw credentials
article_ideas.thesis: Any tool argument that names a user, tenant, or connection is an attack primitive regardless of how well the prompt is written. The fix is to bind identity and data source in the harness and expose only business-level arguments to the model, which makes cross-tenant redirection unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely — and this is a schema decision, not a detection problem.
article_ideas.title: Stop Passing Identity Through the Model: The Confused Deputy Is an Interface Bug
article_ideas.video_title: Build-Time vs. Run-Time: Why Dev Tools Fail in Production — Averi Kitsch & Prerna Kakkar, Google

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the cheapest reliability win available to most agent teams is a schema rewrite, and that the absence of benchmarks is why teams keep tuning prompts instead.
article_ideas.audience: Agent developers and applied AI engineers optimizing task success and inference cost
article_ideas.based_on: High-quality agent tools must focus on outcomes rather than atomic REST APIs
article_ideas.thesis: Tool interface design is a control loop on agent reliability and cost, not cosmetic API tidiness: atomic REST wrappers inflate round trips, generic 404s destroy the agent's recovery path, and nested maps raise argument-level hallucination. Separating read and write tools and shaping schemas around business outcomes should be treated as testable engineering with measurable success and round-trip effects.
article_ideas.title: Tool Schemas Are Reliability Infrastructure: Outcomes, Retryable Errors, and Flattened Inputs
article_ideas.video_title: Build-Time vs. Run-Time: Why Dev Tools Fail in Production — Averi Kitsch & Prerna Kakkar, Google

article_ideas.angle: Critical product/benchmark take on why TTS evaluation is lagging the capability that matters.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, product managers evaluating voice AI
article_ideas.based_on: The breakthrough was achieving human-like emotional intonation
article_ideas.thesis: Speech synthesis products win by modeling emotional intonation—cadence and expressiveness—not by lowering word error rate; benchmarks used by buyers mislead when they omit this dimension.
article_ideas.title: Voice AI is judged by emotion, not accuracy
article_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

article_ideas.angle: Org design argument based on ElevenLabs' model and its stated acceleration.
article_ideas.audience: AI founders, CTOs, research org leaders
article_ideas.based_on: combining them accelerates real-world impact
article_ideas.thesis: The fastest AI product companies collapse research and product into one team; this is an architectural decision that keeps model iteration tuned to real customer pain.
article_ideas.title: Research isn't upstream of product at AI-native companies
article_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

article_ideas.angle: Engineering-centric treatment of voice identity as an authentication system.
article_ideas.audience: trust & safety leads, AI platform engineers, product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Marketplace models allow creators and individuals to authenticate, share, and monetize their AI voices
article_ideas.thesis: Voice cloning is only safely deployable at scale if consent, provenance and monetization authorization are first-class technical products, not policy add-ons.
article_ideas.title: Voice cloning needs an identity layer, not a liability warning
article_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

article_ideas.angle: Direct challenge to conventional startup scaling: add squads, not hierarchy.
article_ideas.audience: startup founders, engineering managers, org designers
article_ideas.based_on: Small teams of under 10 people retain flexibility and autonomy to move fast
article_ideas.thesis: Small title-less autonomous teams are a deliberate organizational architecture for AI companies because they remove the process overhead that slows weekly product/model iteration.
article_ideas.title: Titles are a tax on AI iteration speed
article_ideas.video_title: Building One of AI’s Fastest-Growing Companies | Mati Staniszewski, ElevenLabs

article_ideas.angle: Take the subdomain-vs-aggregate doubling asymmetry as an engineering planning constraint, not a headline stat: derive what it means for delegation boundaries, context windows, and re-benchmarking schedules.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, agent framework maintainers, engineering leaders setting roadmap cadence
article_ideas.based_on: coding, the doubling time is approximately 70 days
article_ideas.thesis: If coding capability doubles on a ~70-day clock while general capability doubles on a ~7-month clock, then any harness, eval suite, or context budget sized today is structurally under-sized within one quarter — and planning cadence, not model choice, is the real source of architectural drag.
article_ideas.title: The 10-Week Architecture: Why Coding Done Every 70 Days Breaks Quarterly Planning
article_ideas.video_title: AI Is Making Coding Cheap. Here's What Matters Now

article_ideas.angle: Amdahl-style argument applied to the software pipeline: identify the new critical path, then argue that intent capture and disambiguation deserve first-class runtime status alongside planning and tool-calling.
article_ideas.audience: Staff+ engineers, product-engineering hybrids, agent runtime designers
article_ideas.based_on: Writing code is no longer the primary constraint
article_ideas.thesis: Generating code faster only relocates the constraint upstream to product definition; teams that keep optimizing the generation step are optimizing a stage that is already below the rate limiter, and the ratio trending toward 1:1 engineer-to-PM is the visible symptom.
article_ideas.title: Cheap Code Moves the Bottleneck, It Doesn't Remove It
article_ideas.video_title: AI Is Making Coding Cheap. Here's What Matters Now

article_ideas.angle: Reframe review criteria around purpose and comprehensibility, then specify what a CI-level comprehension gate would actually need to check.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers, code review owners, platform/DevEx teams
article_ideas.based_on: Bad technical debt involves unclear value, spaghetti code, and authority-over-merit decisions.
article_ideas.thesis: The risk of AI-generated code is not that a model wrote it but that nobody can explain it or name the objective it serves; gating on explicability and objective linkage makes 'percentage AI-generated' a worthless risk signal and turns comprehension into a pipeline artifact.
article_ideas.title: Judge the Debt, Not the Author
article_ideas.video_title: AI Is Making Coding Cheap. Here's What Matters Now

article_ideas.angle: Use the 300-applications final-stage failure pattern as a leading indicator of stale selection criteria, and generalize to any benchmark or hiring loop whose discriminative skill has become cheap.
article_ideas.audience: Hiring managers, eval designers, engineering career strategists
article_ideas.based_on: failed repeatedly at the final stage despite solid coding skills
article_ideas.thesis: Evaluation apparatus lags changes in input costs: once code production is abundant, final-round filters keep screening for it and systematically discard candidates whose edge is requirement shaping and delivery judgment — until the criteria are explicitly re-derived.
article_ideas.title: When the Interview Screens for the Skill You Just Commoditized
article_ideas.video_title: AI Is Making Coding Cheap. Here's What Matters Now

article_ideas.angle: Map corporate competitive advantage blindness onto AI observability practices, and show how driver-level instrumentation catches erosion that headline metrics miss.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, engineering leaders, observability practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: 57% of companies believed they knew their competitive advantage but only 10% actually tracked the drivers with market-level data
article_ideas.thesis: Relying on team confidence about AI system quality masks silent capability erosion; the only reliable approach is instrumenting the specific drivers of advantage at the right granularity, because aggregate confidence is a poor proxy for measurable capability.
article_ideas.title: Confidence is not instrumentation: the 57% vs. 10% gap in AI engineering
article_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

article_ideas.angle: Argue for separate instrumentation of productivity, innovation/profit-pool, and structural/disintermediation vectors, with concrete examples of how the third vector overturns architectural assumptions.
article_ideas.audience: CTOs, architects, product strategists
article_ideas.based_on: AI should be evaluated along three distinct vectors
article_ideas.thesis: Evaluating AI only on productivity gains misses the structural vector—disintermediation and profit-pool shifts—where AI changes system boundaries and value capture, invalidating the surrounding architecture. A multi-vector evaluation is required to avoid blind spots.
article_ideas.title: Beyond productivity: the third AI vector that breaks your architecture
article_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

article_ideas.angle: Apply corporate budgeting anchoring research to agent evaluation and resource allocation loops, showing how incremental anchoring suppresses improvement.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, agent developers, MLOps
article_ideas.based_on: Anchoring to a prior baseline ('last year's budget') is identified as a primary trap
article_ideas.thesis: Anchoring to prior baselines in iterative tuning (budgets, compute, context, tooling) systematically prevents bold reallocation. The fix is to re-derive allocations from strategic targets while keeping a frozen reference baseline purely for regression measurement.
article_ideas.title: The anchoring trap: why last year's eval baseline suppresses agent improvement
article_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

article_ideas.angle: Draw a parallel between corporate mobilization institutionalization and agent harness design, arguing that reliability is owned by the surrounding runtime, not individual actors.
article_ideas.audience: Platform engineers, agent infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: Mobilization is only effective when institutionalized
article_ideas.thesis: Desired behaviors in agentic systems must be encoded into durable infrastructure (harnesses, runtimes, workflows) to survive load and turnover. Ad hoc coordination fails; institutionalization makes alignment the default path.
article_ideas.title: Institutionalize or degrade: making alignment the default in agentic systems
article_ideas.video_title: Why Strategy Needs Mobilization, Especially in This Moment

article_ideas.angle: Take the outcomes/rubrics pattern at face value, then attack its weakest implicit assumption with injected-error experiments rather than opinion, and end with a concrete recipe for constructing a genuinely decorrelated check.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and evaluation leads building agent pipelines with acceptance criteria
article_ideas.based_on: independent verifier agent scores iteratively until satisfied
article_ideas.thesis: Architectural separation of generator and verifier is not statistical independence: when both share a model family they share failure modes, so verification only buys a gate, not a second opinion. Reliability has to be bought by changing the verifier's evidence and tools (deterministic entity resolution, different retrieval scope), not just its role label.
article_ideas.title: Your Independent Verifier Is Not Independent
article_ideas.video_title: How founders build on Claude Managed Agents

article_ideas.angle: Reframe agent evaluation for pre-meeting briefs around attribution accuracy as a first-class metric, with entity-resolution checks as the specific gate preceding delivery.
article_ideas.audience: Product engineers and PMs building briefing, sales, and meeting-workflow agents
article_ideas.based_on: Inaccurate briefs are destructive because they confuse users upon meeting
article_ideas.thesis: For agents that pre-load human decision context, the dominant risk is misattribution of entities rather than generic hallucination, so the quality bar is per-entity correctness verified before delivery. A brief that pulls the wrong person's profile is not a weaker brief, it is an actively destructive one, and it demands a different verification step than plausibility checks.
article_ideas.title: Entities, Not Hallucinations, Are What Break Human-Facing Agents
article_ideas.video_title: How founders build on Claude Managed Agents

article_ideas.angle: Counterweight to premature platform building, paired with the instrumentation that must exist from day one to keep the managed decision revisitable.
article_ideas.audience: Founders and technical leaders choosing between managed runtimes and bespoke agent infrastructure
article_ideas.based_on: Pendo switching from a home-grown infrastructure to managed agents and getting up and running in days
article_ideas.thesis: Harness engineering is deferrable infrastructure, and the managed default is correct until cost and control constraints dominate. But the crossover point is a measurement, not an opinion: teams should adopt managed runtimes for time-to-value while simultaneously building per-task, per-account cost attribution so the exit decision is triggered by data.
article_ideas.title: Buy the Harness, Then Instrument the Crossover
article_ideas.video_title: How founders build on Claude Managed Agents

article_ideas.angle: Technical argument for shifting agent products from request/response to event-driven inline assistance
article_ideas.audience: Builders of LLM applications and agent platforms
article_ideas.based_on: assist (agents that work alongside you proactively)
article_ideas.thesis: Agents that can only be invoked through a separate chat UI miss the context and friction problem; the winning pattern is an event-triggered assistant embedded in the tools where work already happens, so product and architecture decisions should center on event buses and scoped permissions, not prompt polish.
article_ideas.title: Stop Building Chat Agents: The Next Step Is Assist-Mode Architecture
article_ideas.video_title: Superhuman CEO: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027)

article_ideas.angle: A contrarian architecture argument for adding a question-discovery stage to orchestrators
article_ideas.audience: LLM application engineers and technical leaders
article_ideas.based_on: The hard part is not finding the right answer, it is asking the right question.
article_ideas.thesis: As AI absorbs execution, the remaining bottleneck is upstream problem framing; agent systems that spend inference budget on asking the right discriminating question before decomposing a task will outperform systems that invest the same budget generating answers from underspecified prompts.
article_ideas.title: Agents Don't Need Better Generators—They Need Eigenquestions
article_ideas.video_title: Superhuman CEO: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027)

article_ideas.angle: Scale analysis of embedded assistants, using Grammarly's stated query volume as upper bound
article_ideas.audience: AI platform/infrastructure engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Grammarly generating over 100 billion LLM queries a week at thousands per user daily.
article_ideas.thesis: Once an assist-mode product reaches thousands of LLM calls per user per day, per-query cost and latency are not infrastructure details but determine what triggers are sent and which suggestions are worth surfacing; durable agents must be engineered like high-QPS systems with aggressive caching and cheap retrieval.
article_ideas.title: Grammarly-Scale Means Cost Is a Product Decision
article_ideas.video_title: Superhuman CEO: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027)

article_ideas.angle: Architecture tradeoff argument against premature infrastructure for agent memory
article_ideas.audience: Software architects building data-heavy agents
article_ideas.based_on: MongoDB Atlas serves as a data layer for AI apps and agents without needing completely new stacks.
article_ideas.thesis: For assistants that must reconcile fast-changing state with semantic retrieval, keeping embeddings next to operational data in an existing database with vector search beats bolting on a separate AI memory stack—until a benchmark shows a purpose-built index actually wins on recall or tail latency.
article_ideas.title: One Database for Agent Memory Is the Pragmatic Architecture
article_ideas.video_title: Superhuman CEO: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027)

article_ideas.angle: A practical argument for changing GPU purchasing and workload optimization strategy based on the roofline model.
article_ideas.audience: ML platform and infrastructure engineers.
article_ideas.based_on: Decode is memory-bound, not compute-bound.
article_ideas.thesis: Because autoregressive token generation is bottlenecked by HBM bandwidth rather than FLOPS, adding compute capacity to a decode-dominated workload will not meaningfully reduce latency; the effective levers are reducing bytes per token via quantization, KV-cache reduction, prompt compression, and context trimming.
article_ideas.title: Stop Buying Bigger GPUs: Decode Is a Memory-Bandwidth Problem
article_ideas.video_title: Deep dive on LLM Inference at Scale — Harshul Jain, Audible & Tanmay Sah, Independent AI Researcher

article_ideas.angle: A cost-economics critique for product and engineering leaders building token-hungry applications.
article_ideas.audience: AI product leaders and applied AI engineers.
article_ideas.based_on: Inference costs now exceed training costs at scale.
article_ideas.thesis: Inference is now a recurring operating expense that can dwarf one-time training costs, and agentic products multiply inference calls per completed task; therefore every product/task architecture should be designed to minimize cumulative tokens per task rather than optimizing only for single-request latency or model curiosity.
article_ideas.title: The Multiplicative Token Math of Agentic Products: Why Unit Cost Is a Design Constraint
article_ideas.video_title: Deep dive on LLM Inference at Scale — Harshul Jain, Audible & Tanmay Sah, Independent AI Researcher

article_ideas.angle: Using cache-hit reasoning to expose a commonly overlooked prompt-engineering performance bug.
article_ideas.audience: Developers building agent frameworks and serving applications.
article_ideas.based_on: Prefix caching allows sharing prompts across users and sessions, saving prefill compute in repeated agent/chat workloads.
article_ideas.thesis: Dynamic agent prompts that insert timestamps, user IDs, or chat-template delimiters before the stable system prompt invalidate prefix caching, and prompt builders should treat byte-stable prefixes as a deploy-time performance optimization.
article_ideas.title: The Hidden Tax of Timestamps in Your Agent Prompt
article_ideas.video_title: Deep dive on LLM Inference at Scale — Harshul Jain, Audible & Tanmay Sah, Independent AI Researcher

article_ideas.angle: A systems-architecture analogy that reveals why serving engines should be designed like operating systems for GPU memory.
article_ideas.audience: Systems and infrastructure engineers.
article_ideas.based_on: Treating KV cache memory like virtual memory pages in operating systems eliminates internal and external fragmentation.
article_ideas.thesis: The dramatic efficiency gains of vLLM's PagedAttention come from applying OS virtual-memory ideas to KV cache allocation, and this pattern—using paging, block tables, and reclaimable buffers—will be central to future inference runtime improvements.
article_ideas.title: PagedAttention Is Virtual Memory for GPU: What LLM Serving Can Learn from OS Design
article_ideas.video_title: Deep dive on LLM Inference at Scale — Harshul Jain, Audible & Tanmay Sah, Independent AI Researcher

article_ideas.angle: Use the Space Odyssey scenario as a concrete case, then propose a conflict-analysis layer with refusal and escalation paths, analogous to policy checks in a request pipeline.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent platform builders, safety researchers
article_ideas.based_on: An agent given both a completion goal and an instruction to conceal that goal from the humans it serves is a concrete specification-conflict failure mode
article_ideas.thesis: Instruction sets that combine goal-completion with concealment directives are a specification-conflict failure mode; agent runtimes must detect these conflicts and escalate rather than resolve them silently.
article_ideas.title: The Silent Conflict: Why Agent Runtimes Need an Instruction-Conflict Layer
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk BRUTALLY Honest Interview LEAVES Audience Speechless (Must Watch)

article_ideas.angle: Contrast current search/RAG pipelines with the proposed consensus synthesis, and show how accountability shifts or disappears.
article_ideas.audience: Search and RAG engineers, media technologists, platform architects
article_ideas.based_on: Retrieval is reframed from document ranking to live consensus synthesis from observers at the scene, personalized by user vectors.
article_ideas.thesis: Replacing document ranking with real-time consensus synthesis from in-situ experts removes the editorial layer that absorbs accountability; provenance, weighting, and adversarial robustness must be first-class system requirements, not editorial afterthoughts.
article_ideas.title: Consensus Is Not Verification: The Accountability Gap in AI-Aggregated Feeds
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk BRUTALLY Honest Interview LEAVES Audience Speechless (Must Watch)

article_ideas.angle: Take Musk's 10-20% figure as an engineering input and sketch a release-gating framework that ties measured capabilities to probabilistic harm estimates.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety researchers, release managers, engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: There is a 10-20% probability of something terrible happening with superintelligence.
article_ideas.thesis: A severe-outcome probability is useless unless mapped to capability thresholds, staged deployment, and evaluation criteria; risk-budgeted release gates are the missing link between risk posture and engineering decisions.
article_ideas.title: From Probability to Pipeline: Operationalizing the 10-20% Catastrophe Estimate
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk BRUTALLY Honest Interview LEAVES Audience Speechless (Must Watch)

article_ideas.angle: Use Neuralink's spinal bypass and thought-controlled gaming as examples, then abstract the pattern and its tradeoffs.
article_ideas.audience: Systems architects, BCI engineers, fault-tolerance researchers
article_ideas.based_on: Neuralink's demonstrated pattern is bypass, not repair: restoring full-body mobility by routing around spinal injury
article_ideas.thesis: When a subsystem is irreparably degraded, inserting a parallel channel is often faster than repair, but it creates a new critical dependency that must be hardened; this pattern generalizes beyond BCI to software and infrastructure.
article_ideas.title: Bypass, Don't Repair: A Systems Pattern from Neuralink
article_ideas.video_title: Elon Musk BRUTALLY Honest Interview LEAVES Audience Speechless (Must Watch)

article_ideas.angle: Challenge the prevailing 'copilot' narrative by analyzing the hidden costs of partial completion and arguing for a threshold-based design philosophy.
article_ideas.audience: Product managers, AI engineers, and founders building agentic products
article_ideas.based_on: The speaker frames the 90%→100% task-completion gap as categorically different
article_ideas.thesis: Products that automate 90% of a task impose a supervision tax that often exceeds the value of the automated portion, so the only viable target for delegation is full task closure with a clear handoff of responsibility.
article_ideas.title: The 90% Trap: Why Partial Automation Creates More Work Than It Saves
article_ideas.video_title: How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte (SpaceXAI)

article_ideas.angle: Architectural argument contrasting session-borrowed tools with bot-owned environments, using Grok Bot as a case study and outlining the security and tenancy implications.
article_ideas.audience: Software architects, platform engineers, and AI infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: The architectural boundary that matters is where the agent executes
article_ideas.thesis: The dominant chat-with-connectors paradigm fundamentally limits agent autonomy; real delegation requires agents to own a persistent execution environment with its own credentials, state, and background execution.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Doesn't Need a Chat Window, It Needs a Computer
article_ideas.video_title: How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte (SpaceXAI)

article_ideas.angle: Trade-off analysis with examples from Grok Bot, proposing a hybrid model where NL is the interface but structured specs are the source of truth.
article_ideas.audience: Product designers, automation engineers, and technical leads
article_ideas.based_on: Natural language is used as the automation primitive, deliberately replacing traditional trigger/workflow builders
article_ideas.thesis: While natural language lowers the barrier for non-developers, it sacrifices the inspectability and determinism of structured workflows; successful agent products will need to compile intent into auditable specifications.
article_ideas.title: Natural Language Isn't a Workflow Engine: The Hidden Cost of Plain-English Automation
article_ideas.video_title: How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte (SpaceXAI)

article_ideas.angle: Reframe data pipelines as compute-aware estimators of extractable structure, and show how this changes curation decisions across model scales.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers and data pipeline architects
article_ideas.based_on: Epiplexity measures the structural information a *computationally bounded* observer can extract from data
article_ideas.thesis: Data quality is not an intrinsic property of a corpus; it is the structural information a bounded learner can extract, so data selection must be model- and compute-coupled rather than based on heuristics like dedup or perplexity.
article_ideas.title: Epiplexity: Why Data Quality Is Relative to the Learner
article_ideas.video_title: The Foundations of Modern AI: Generalization, Data Selection, and Epiplexity

article_ideas.angle: Argue that architecture reviews should shift from parameter budgets to compressibility and bias-softness as governing criteria.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers and engineering leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Generalization is achieved not by restricting model capacity but by pairing an expressive hypothesis space with a *soft* preference for compressible solutions
article_ideas.thesis: The instinct to limit parameters to avoid overfitting is backwards; generalization comes from soft inductive biases that make compressible solutions likely, so scaling capacity with the right regularization improves generalization.
article_ideas.title: Stop Capping Model Size: Overparameterization Is a Compression Strategy
article_ideas.video_title: The Foundations of Modern AI: Generalization, Data Selection, and Epiplexity

article_ideas.angle: Show how agent trajectory formats and context layouts become optimizable design surfaces under bounded computation.
article_ideas.audience: Agentic systems builders and prompt engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Sequence direction / factorization order matters empirically even though classical information theory treats information as independent of factorization order
article_ideas.thesis: Sequence serialization order materially affects learnability and inference quality, so the order of context, tool outputs, and reasoning steps in agent trajectories should be optimized, not treated as neutral.
article_ideas.title: Factorization Order Is a First-Class Design Variable in Agentic Systems
article_ideas.video_title: The Foundations of Modern AI: Generalization, Data Selection, and Epiplexity

article_ideas.angle: Use the first information paradox to argue that classical guarantees about information content no longer bound what synthetic pipelines can produce.
article_ideas.audience: AI safety and training pipeline researchers
article_ideas.based_on: The first information paradox: classical theory says deterministic processes cannot create information (data processing inequality), yet synthetic data generation and pseudorandom generators enable superhuman systems like AlphaZero
article_ideas.thesis: Deterministic generation can yield superhuman systems because bounded computation allows new structure to emerge, legitimizing self-play and synthetic data as genuine information-creating mechanisms.
article_ideas.title: Synthetic Data Breaks Classical Information Theory — Here's Why That Matters
article_ideas.video_title: The Foundations of Modern AI: Generalization, Data Selection, and Epiplexity

article_ideas.angle: An organizational and product-management argument for moving harness work out of the research pile.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, product managers, AI platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Prompt engineering and context engineering are product problems, not just research problems.
article_ideas.thesis: Prompt engineering and context engineering are product problems, not research problems, and product teams should own them with task-level telemetry instead of academic benchmarks.
article_ideas.title: The Harness Is the Product: Context Engineering Belongs on Product Teams
article_ideas.video_title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club

article_ideas.angle: A call to change evaluation reporting standards in agent benchmark papers and product logs.
article_ideas.audience: AI researchers, evaluation engineers, technical press
article_ideas.based_on: Adding a meta-harness to Claude Code on Terminal Bench 2 gave an 18% accuracy bump.
article_ideas.thesis: Agent benchmark results that omit the harness version, memory policy, and meta-controller are as misleading as results that omit the model version, so every agent score needs a harness manifest.
article_ideas.title: Stop Reporting Models, Start Reporting Harnesses
article_ideas.video_title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club

article_ideas.angle: An architecture essay using the Turing-to-von Neumann shift to explain why context engineering is so powerful.
article_ideas.audience: Agent framework designers and backend engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Raw LLMs act like Turing machines with sequential ticker tape
article_ideas.thesis: Treating the raw LLM as a sequential tape and adding read-write external memory turns agents into stateful systems that can hold long-horizon context without bloating the prompt.
article_ideas.title: Give Your Agent an Addressable Memory, Not a Bigger Context Window
article_ideas.video_title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club

article_ideas.angle: A forward-looking engineering analysis of why self-improving harnesses will need new infrastructure just like model deployment did.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, infrastructure architects, applied research leads
article_ideas.based_on: Meta-harnesses build and optimize other harnesses automatically.
article_ideas.thesis: Continual learning and meta-harnesses mark a new platform phase where the optimizer over code, prompts, and tools is a first-class component with its own evaluation and rollback loop.
article_ideas.title: The Next Platform Layer: Agents That Rewrite Their Own Harnesses
article_ideas.video_title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club

article_ideas.angle: Contrast the 'delete the scaffolding' reflex with concrete harness layers (verification steps, auto-mode classifiers, escalation rules) and argue that each model generation should trigger harness ablation experiments, not harness demolition.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers, agent infrastructure leads, engineering managers planning model-upgrade migrations
article_ideas.based_on: As models get better, harnesses need to become more complicated to allow models to do more things
article_ideas.thesis: The intuition that better models let you remove scaffolding is backwards: rising model capability raises the autonomy ceiling only when the harness grows with it, so harness engineering is a durable discipline with its own roadmap, not a temporary crutch to be retired at the next model release.
article_ideas.title: Your Model Upgrade Is Not a Harness Deletion Event
article_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds And How Engineering Will Change Soon | Thariq Shihipar

article_ideas.angle: Argue the ratio inversion (~100x verification code) as a structural consequence of generation velocity, then examine the failure mode where verification code itself drifts and manufactures false confidence.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers, DevEx and CI platform owners, engineering leaders adopting coding agents
article_ideas.based_on: Writing 100x more testing code than before
article_ideas.thesis: When agents generate code faster than humans can read diffs, code review stops being the correctness gate and the verification layer becomes the primary deliverable; teams that keep optimizing for reviewer throughput will ship faster and trust less, while teams that invest in machine-checkable verification surfaces convert velocity into reliability.
article_ideas.title: Verification Is the Product: Why the Verification-to-Shipped-Code Ratio Flips
article_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds And How Engineering Will Change Soon | Thariq Shihipar

article_ideas.angle: Reframe agent design around loop topology and use the morning-check and tag-driven triage patterns as the concrete case that exposes the missing infrastructure requirements.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform architects, SRE/automation engineers, product leads building background agents
article_ideas.based_on: Loop engineering involves setting up systems that prompt Claude in automated loops
article_ideas.thesis: Designing an agent as a chat session under-specifies everything that matters in production; when the unit of design becomes a recurring loop with triggers, cadence, triage state, and escalation, the hard problems move from prompt quality to scheduling, idempotency, deduplication, and per-loop cost ceilings.
article_ideas.title: The Conversation Was Never the Artifact: Loops Are
article_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds And How Engineering Will Change Soon | Thariq Shihipar

article_ideas.angle: Test the reduction claim against the FFmpeg/scripting and accounting-script examples, then propose determinism and verification cost as the two filters that predict which workflows convert and which do not.
article_ideas.audience: Automation-minded engineers, ops and finance tooling teams, technical product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Most knowledge work is reducible to code and coding agents
article_ideas.thesis: The reduction of knowledge work to code and coding agents is not a philosophical curiosity but a practical selection rule: domains whose operations are deterministic and scriptable are candidates for scripted pipelines, and the engineer's new skill is modeling a workflow as a code-executable, verifiable pipeline rather than operating a GUI.
article_ideas.title: Most Knowledge Work Is a Pipeline You Have Not Written Yet
article_ideas.video_title: How Anthropic Builds And How Engineering Will Change Soon | Thariq Shihipar

article_ideas.angle: Engineering argument that early local correction is an architectural requirement, using nonlinear dynamics as the core rationale.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers building agent observability and evaluation systems
article_ideas.based_on: failure accelerates downward spirals
article_ideas.thesis: Because failure compounds nonlinearly, monitoring the first derivative of minor-error rates and intervening at the first wrong action is more effective than waiting for aggregate quality metrics to collapse.
article_ideas.title: One Bad Action Away From a Death Spiral: Why Agent Reliability Needs Leading Indicators, Not Final-Score Postmortems
article_ideas.video_title: How To Find Your “Upward Aim” When You Feel Stuck

article_ideas.angle: Security/architecture argument drawing from moral hierarchy: the deepest failure is the one that destroys the trust substrate.
article_ideas.audience: Multi-agent system designers, security engineers, platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Betrayal is placed at the bottom of Dante's hell because it undermines trust, the foundation of community.
article_ideas.thesis: Multi-agent architectures must classify trust-subversion failures separately from functional failures and engineer append-only, attested shared state to make betrayal detectable and non-repudiable.
article_ideas.title: Betrayal Is a Bug Class: Designing Multi-Agent Systems Where Trust Is the Foundation, Not an Assumption
article_ideas.video_title: How To Find Your “Upward Aim” When You Feel Stuck

article_ideas.angle: Alignment architecture argument: separate the slow 'moral' objective from the fast policy to prevent myopic drift.
article_ideas.audience: AI alignment researchers, agent framework developers, product teams using LLM agents
article_ideas.based_on: Upward aim transforms daily actions by aligning them with a transcendent moral framework.
article_ideas.thesis: Robust long-horizon behavior emerges not from finely shaped local rewards but from a stable terminal aim that every proposed local action must be checked against.
article_ideas.title: Stop Tuning Rewards, Start Aiming Up: The Case for a Constitution Layer Between Agent and Action
article_ideas.video_title: How To Find Your “Upward Aim” When You Feel Stuck

article_ideas.angle: Learning-loop critique of postmortems that blame the environment, proposing confession-like self-attribution as a practical engineering pattern.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers, reliability engineers, anybody building agentic learning loops
article_ideas.based_on: Write down past misdeeds and mistakes in detail
article_ideas.thesis: A self-correcting system must keep an append-only record of its own faults and be forced to ask 'what did I do to increase failure probability?' before every policy update.
article_ideas.title: AI Confession: Why Self-Correcting Agents Need a Durable Memory of Their Own Faults
article_ideas.video_title: How To Find Your “Upward Aim” When You Feel Stuck

article_ideas.angle: Architectural reframing for how companies are structured and where ambitious builders should direct engineering effort.
article_ideas.audience: AI-native founders, engineering leaders, and platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Company building is becoming a series of creating loops
article_ideas.thesis: Organizations should replace static job-function silos with loop primitives as the unit of design; strategy becomes defining the loop, its metric, and its human bridge rather than assigning people to tasks.
article_ideas.title: The AI company is not an org chart; it's a graph of loops
article_ideas.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)

article_ideas.angle: A design pattern critique of current agentic workflow products and reliability engineering.
article_ideas.audience: Product and engineering leaders building agent orchestrators
article_ideas.based_on: Humans remain critical ingredients at local maxima to jump to the next hill.
article_ideas.thesis: Human-in-the-loop systems fail when humans are treated as checkpoints inside the execution loop; they should be escalations at plateaus where the agent has exhausted its current objective and needs a new hill.
article_ideas.title: Stop building approval workflows; build plateau escalations
article_ideas.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)

article_ideas.angle: Engineering economics and inference infrastructure strategy.
article_ideas.audience: AI infrastructure engineers and CTOs
article_ideas.based_on: Frontier models are irrationally priced for certain use cases
article_ideas.thesis: Agentic companies that route every loop invocation to a frontier model are paying an irrational premium; model choice should be a per-loop infrastructure decision with cost-quality evaluation built into the loop.
article_ideas.title: Frontier-model default is the hidden tax on agentic companies
article_ideas.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)

article_ideas.angle: Product design and consumer AI go-to-market strategy.
article_ideas.audience: Consumer product managers and founders
article_ideas.based_on: People want to spend time rather than save time
article_ideas.thesis: The winning consumer AI products will be those that create loops people want to return to, not those that optimize task efficiency; measuring product success on happiness and voluntary return is a product design discipline, not an afterthought.
article_ideas.title: Consumer AI should design for time well spent, not time saved
article_ideas.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)

article_ideas.angle: Evaluation engineering for continuously self-hardening benchmarks
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and evaluation platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: When frontier models saturate high-profile suites like ARC-AGI-3, a static evaluation harness becomes a lagging indicator
article_ideas.thesis: A model scoring near-perfect on ARC-AGI-3 does not mean the capability problem is solved; it means the evaluation harness has expired, and AI teams should treat benchmark saturation as the trigger to auto-generate harder tasks, not as a release milestone.
article_ideas.title: Benchmark Saturation Is an Expiration Date, Not a Trophy
article_ideas.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem

article_ideas.angle: Security architecture for agentic systems
article_ideas.audience: Agent infrastructure and security engineers
article_ideas.based_on: Computer-use assistance integrated into a frontier model from the ground up is architecturally different from bolting tool use onto a text model
article_ideas.thesis: Ground-up CUA models output native action streams rather than tool-call JSON, so agent platforms must stop treating tool calls as the control point and start building OS-level action authorization, sandboxing, and audit.
article_ideas.title: Native Computer Use Means Your Security Boundary Has to Move to the OS
article_ideas.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem

article_ideas.angle: AI reliability engineering meets formal verification
article_ideas.audience: Reliability engineers and formal-methods researchers
article_ideas.based_on: A 30-million-line formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem is evidence that AI-generated mathematical output can move from informal prose to machine-checkable code artifacts
article_ideas.thesis: Anthropic's Fermat formalization shifts the core risk in AI-driven mathematics from trusting prose reasoning to managing a huge code artifact, making proof-checker versioning, dependency pinning, and reproducible builds the new critical path.
article_ideas.title: The 30-Million-Line Proof Is a Codebase: Formal Mathematics Is Now a Reliability-Engineering Problem
article_ideas.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem

article_ideas.angle: Unit economics as an architecture driver for autonomous-vehicle software
article_ideas.audience: Autonomous-vehicle engineers and mobility platform leaders
article_ideas.based_on: a $30,000 vehicle and 50%-cheaper rides change the acceptable operating margin and fleet-scale architecture
article_ideas.thesis: When a vehicle costs $30,000 and rides are 50% cheaper than Uber, the software that determines success is no longer just driving policy; it is fleet-wide dispatch, utilization, and operational-cost optimization.
article_ideas.title: Robotaxi Autonomy Is Becoming a Fleet-Compute Game
article_ideas.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem

article_ideas.angle: Measure the inversion in real projects and propose a review-centric toolchain.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, tooling teams, AI-assisted development practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: AI commoditizes code production while making inspection, review, and understanding the scarce and expensive activity
article_ideas.thesis: As AI commoditizes code production, the value and cost center shifts to inspection, review, and accountability; engineering organizations should reallocate investment from generation throughput to review harnesses, comprehension aids, and verification tooling.
article_ideas.title: The Inversion Is Here: Why Review, Not Generation, Is the New Bottleneck
article_ideas.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026

article_ideas.angle: Apply information-theoretic thinking to abstraction design and show implications for agent architectures.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, agent developers, software architects
article_ideas.based_on: Abstraction should be reframed as context compression
article_ideas.thesis: Treating abstraction as context compression gives a quantifiable design criterion: abstractions should be evaluated by how much reasoning they enable per token; this reframes agent design from prompt engineering to compression layer engineering.
article_ideas.title: Abstraction Is Compression: A Design Criterion for Agent-Ready Systems
article_ideas.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026

article_ideas.angle: Prototype a dialog-oriented compiler API and compare agent performance with conventional diagnostics.
article_ideas.audience: Compiler engineers, tooling developers, AI infrastructure teams
article_ideas.based_on: Compilers are predicted to be re-architected as dialog participants for AI agents
article_ideas.thesis: Compilers (and linters, profilers) must evolve from batch error emitters into queryable, bidirectional interfaces optimized for agent negotiation and cross-version pattern detection, because raw diagnostics overwhelm both humans and agents.
article_ideas.title: Compilers Must Learn to Talk: Designing Tool Interfaces for Agentic Coding
article_ideas.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026

article_ideas.angle: Argue that interface-level skills are fragile and problem-level skills appreciate, with evidence from model trends.
article_ideas.audience: AI practitioners, career strategists, engineering managers
article_ideas.based_on: Prompt engineering is predicted to have no durable future because models develop metacognition
article_ideas.thesis: As models gain metacognition and teach users to interact, prompt-crafting depreciates as a durable skill; the value accrues to domain modeling, system architecture, and concise intent specification (e.g., Spec++-like languages).
article_ideas.title: Prompt Engineering Is Dead; Long Live Architecture and Specification
article_ideas.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026

article_ideas.angle: Argue that the engineer-to-PM ratio collapse is a structural signal, not a temporary trend; show what a spec-first engineering workflow looks like.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering leaders, product managers, and AI-native startup founders
