deep_dives.topic: Plateau detection and human retargeting in autonomous loops
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Humans remain critical ingredients at local maxima to jump to the next hill.
deep_dives.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)
deep_dives.why: Human review at every step is expensive and undermines the economics of autonomous loops; the missing capability is knowing when to interrupt a human with a well-formed decision about the next hill to climb.

evidence_quotes.text: People want to spend time rather than save time.
The challenge in consumer AI is a product design challenge, not a model capability challenge.

deep_dives.research_question: How does emotional need satisfaction — fun, connection, progress, love — causally affect voluntary return and engagement in consumer AI products compared with task-completion utility?
deep_dives.topic: Consumer AI product loops as time-spending desire satisfaction
deep_dives.trigger_insight: People want to spend time rather than save time.
deep_dives.video_title: Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya (a16z)
deep_dives.why: If people want to spend time rather than save it, consumer AI evaluation must move beyond task-efficiency metrics and measure experiential loops designed around human desire.

evidence_quotes.text: Abstraction is context compression.
Larger project scales require better abstractions to manage cognitive load.
The more you know, the less creativity you need because existing patterns guide solutions.

deep_dives.research_question: Can the compression ratio of an abstraction be quantified, and does higher compression predict better reasoning performance under fixed context budgets?
deep_dives.topic: Quantifying abstraction as context compression
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Abstraction should be reframed as context compression
deep_dives.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026
deep_dives.why: Abstraction is posited as context compression, but without metrics we cannot compare abstraction designs or predict how much system an agent can reason about within a token budget. A compression metric would make abstraction a first-class engineering variable.

evidence_quotes.text: Code production is commoditized by AI tools.
The onus has shifted from writing code to review, understanding, and responsibility.
Fluency in syntax is de-emphasized; producing is cheap, inspecting is expensive.

deep_dives.research_question: Do measured time-and-cost distributions in real AI-assisted projects actually shift from generation to review and comprehension, and what tooling best addresses the new bottleneck?
deep_dives.topic: The inversion of cost: measuring the shift from generation to inspection
deep_dives.trigger_insight: AI commoditizes code production while making inspection, review, and understanding the scarce and expensive activity
deep_dives.video_title: Software Abstraction in the Age of AI-Generated Code - Andrei Alexandrescu - ACCU 2026
deep_dives.why: If code production is commoditized and review becomes the expensive activity, investment priorities in tooling, process, and training must invert. Without measurement, we risk over-investing in generation.

evidence_quotes.text: GPT-6 Astra saturates ARC-AGI-3 with near-perfect scores.
Benchmarks need to be continually hardened as AI outpaces traditional evaluation frameworks.

deep_dives.research_question: Can an evaluation harness automatically synthesize new benchmark tasks from a model's own failures quickly enough to prevent saturation on static suites, and what contamination controls are needed to keep those generated tasks trustworthy?
deep_dives.topic: Continuous adversarial benchmark generation for agentic systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: When frontier models saturate high-profile suites like ARC-AGI-3, a static evaluation harness becomes a lagging indicator rather than an engineering guardrail

evidence_quotes.text: Astra integrates computer use assistance (CUA) from the ground up.
Altman noted Astra represents a new frontier model step, carrying critical tier cybersecurity classification.

deep_dives.research_question: What action-level authorization, sandboxing, and audit interceptions can prevent irreversible or dual-use behavior when a model like Astra is trained to produce native computer-use actions rather than intermediary tool-call JSON?
deep_dives.topic: Security boundary design for native computer-use models
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Computer-use assistance integrated into a frontier model from the ground up is architecturally different from bolting tool use onto a text model
deep_dives.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem
deep_dives.why: Ground-up CUA means the model's outputs are already environment commands, so existing tool-call parsing guardrails no longer sit at the correct layer and the entire security model must be re-placed at the OS/action level.

evidence_quotes.text: Anthropic formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 million lines of code.
Proves 29,000 theorems on the way.

deep_dives.research_question: What proof-checker pinning, dependency management, and provenance practices make a 30-million-line machine-generated formal proof independently checkable and resilient to subtle dependency drift?
deep_dives.topic: Reproducibility engineering for AI-generated formal proofs
deep_dives.trigger_insight: A 30-million-line formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem is evidence that AI-generated mathematical output can move from informal prose to machine-checkable code artifacts
deep_dives.video_title: GPT-6 Astra Saturates ARC-AGI-3, Tesla Cybercab Hits Austin, Anthropic Proves Fermat's Last Theorem
deep_dives.why: If mathematical results are now machine-checkable code artifacts, the reliability bottleneck shifts from judging natural-language arguments to maintaining reproducible build and verification environments.

evidence_quotes.text: As coding becomes faster and cheaper through AI, the bottleneck shifts from writing code to deciding what to build and writing clear product specs.
The engineering-to-PM ratio is trending downward toward 2:1 or even 1:1.
Engineers who can talk to users, get feedback, and shape products move the fastest.

deep_dives.research_question: Does implementing a structured product-spec and user-feedback loop around AI coding agents reduce the time from user request to validated feature, and by what mechanism?
deep_dives.topic: Spec-first software development as a unit of AI-native engineering productivity
deep_dives.trigger_insight: bottleneck shifts from writing code to deciding what to build
deep_dives.video_title: Prompting Is Dead in 6 Months. Andrew Ng, Stanford
deep_dives.why: Ng predicts the bottleneck shifts from writing code to deciding what to build; this deep dive would quantify whether spec automation or human feedback is the true constraint and what tooling can ease it.

evidence_quotes.text: Every time you build something with AI, you take on technical debt (good debt vs. bad debt).
Vibe coding leading to spaghetti code and unclear value if not backed by fundamentals and business focus.
Developers must thoroughly understand, document, and test generated code rather than mindlessly copy-pasting.

deep_dives.research_question: What change-frequency, defect-density, documentation, and test-completeness signals measured at merge time predict whether AI-generated code becomes compounding bad debt or repayable 'mortgage-style' good debt over 90-180 days?
deep_dives.topic: Operationalizing good vs. bad AI-code debt
deep_dives.trigger_insight: code generated without understanding is bad debt
deep_dives.video_title: Prompting Is Dead in 6 Months. Andrew Ng, Stanford
deep_dives.why: The credit-card/mortgage metaphor is intuitive, but teams need actionable gates to distinguish debt that accelerates products from debt that produces spaghetti code.

evidence_quotes.text: Wiki pages can have scopes that users can control deterministically
All context goes into a company-wide wiki and must have a human's name attached
deterministic scopes and human attribution

deep_dives.research_question: If a wiki page carries deterministic user-controlled scopes, at which point must filtering occur so that the page is provably absent from a lower-privilege user's context — including through summarization, embedding retrieval, and cached derived artifacts?
deep_dives.topic: Scope enforcement placement: index-time vs. query-time filtering and derived-artifact leakage
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Wiki pages can have scopes that users can control deterministically
deep_dives.video_title: Your company brain will leak secrets: how we stopped it for big banks — Tanmai Gopal, PromptQL
deep_dives.why: The entire 'one shared brain for many privilege levels' design rests on scope enforcement being deterministic. If scopes are enforced only at storage or only at the top-k retrieval step, a low-privilege caller can still reconstruct protected content through summaries, embeddings, or cross-page inference — turning the single shared store into a broad leak surface instead of a local one.

evidence_quotes.text: Do not store credentials in the cloud sandbox
storing shared credentials in the sandbox lets low-privilege agents execute high-privilege actions

deep_dives.research_question: What is the blast radius and failure mode set of an identity-aware layer that injects the initiating user's credentials per HTTP/SQL call — and can a low-privilege caller induce it to make a high-privilege call through confused-deputy, token passthrough, or scope-confusion patterns?
deep_dives.topic: Attack surface of the credential-virtualizing proxy (confused deputy, SSRF, scope confusion)
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Inject user credentials at the HTTP/SQL layer dynamically based on the initiating user's identity
deep_dives.video_title: Your company brain will leak secrets: how we stopped it for big banks — Tanmai Gopal, PromptQL
deep_dives.why: Credential virtualization is presented as the fix, but it relocates trust from the sandbox to a new mediation component that sits on every tool and data call. If that component can be confused about who initiated a call, the escalation path returns in a subtler form, and the fix becomes the vulnerable asset.

evidence_quotes.text: AI has changed the startup landscape by introducing massive GPU and token costs.
Technology gets cheaper over time, but compute demands have created new cost structures for startups.

deep_dives.research_question: How should an agent orchestrator make routing, loop-depth, and model-selection decisions to minimize cost per successful task under variable model capabilities?
deep_dives.topic: Inference-aware agent orchestration and unit economics
deep_dives.trigger_insight: per-inference GPU and token costs
deep_dives.video_title: Paul Graham On Startups, Ambition, and Great Founders
deep_dives.why: GPU and token costs recur on every inference, so agent loops and tool calls are no longer free; the design of any multi-step autonomous workflow must expose the variable cost of each step and route cheap work around expensive model calls.

evidence_quotes.text: Technology often starts by imitating simple narrow functions (like a fly's brain) and scales up to complex human capabilities, sometimes starting flawed before becoming optimized.
Start with a narrow, perfect simple capability

deep_dives.research_question: What measurable readiness criteria distinguish a broad-but-flawed agent from one that is ready for production without constant oversight?
deep_dives.topic: Reliability gates for broad-but-flawed agents
deep_dives.trigger_insight: At what point on the 'fly-to-human' trajectory is a system reliable enough to deploy on critical tasks without constant oversight?
deep_dives.video_title: Paul Graham On Startups, Ambition, and Great Founders
deep_dives.why: The fly-to-human trajectory predicts a stage where a multi-capability agent behaves like a flawed human: plausible but unreliable. Production systems need evaluation gates that observe the rate and severity of these failures before granting autonomy.

evidence_quotes.text: The first 15 to 17 years of a founder's life shape their character and resilience.

deep_dives.research_question: Can early-adversity exposure and recovery history be encoded as auditable, bias-resistant features that improve selection of both human founders and AI agents under uncertainty?
deep_dives.topic: Formative-experience evaluation for founders and agents: turning resilience provenance into a signal
deep_dives.trigger_insight: first 15 to 17 years of a founder's life shape their character and resilience
deep_dives.video_title: Former Sequoia Chairman Michael Moritz on Founders: "It's About the First 15 or 16 Years of Life"
deep_dives.why: Moritz treats the first 15-17 years as a predictive window for resilience; if the same logic applies to agents, evaluation should look beyond current benchmarks to training history, early failure exposure, and recovery traces in order to select systems that survive long-horizon stress.

evidence_quotes.text: Google was perceived as a late entry into search.
Sequoia invested 25 million in Google, resulting in one of the best venture returns.

deep_dives.research_question: Under what measurable conditions can a late-entrant model or framework overcome an incumbent's ecosystem and distribution advantage?
deep_dives.topic: When first-movers lose: late-entrant advantage in AI model and agent-stack markets
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Google was perceived as a late entry into search
deep_dives.video_title: Former Sequoia Chairman Michael Moritz on Founders: "It's About the First 15 or 16 Years of Life"
deep_dives.why: Google was judged as late to search and still won; teams and investors risk anchoring on first-mover dominance when evaluating AI infrastructure, leading to strategic lock-in and undervaluing superior late entrants.

evidence_quotes.text: Webvan was a colossal mistake where Sequoia lost 44 million dollars.
Timing and infrastructure readiness can make or break capital-intensive businesses.

deep_dives.research_question: Which infrastructure-maturity metrics (tool reliability, compute unit costs, data interoperability, observability) best predict whether a capital-intensive deployment reaches escape velocity or becomes a Webvan-style burn?
deep_dives.topic: Readiness thresholds for capital-intensive AI/agent systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Webvan was a colossal mistake where Sequoia lost 44 million dollars
deep_dives.video_title: Former Sequoia Chairman Michael Moritz on Founders: "It's About the First 15 or 16 Years of Life"
deep_dives.why: Capital-intensive agent bets can die before their economics work if enabling infrastructure is immature; explicit readiness gates can prevent premature scaling and convert Webvan-style losses into delayed but viable investments.

evidence_quotes.text: Neuroplasticity is driven by errors and friction, not just comfortable success.
Cellular changes in the anterior midcingulate cortex occur when humans do things they do not want to do.

deep_dives.research_question: What error rate and task-difficulty profile maximizes durable adaptation in agent reinforcement learning without provoking reward hacking, learned helplessness, or overfitting?
deep_dives.topic: Error-friction curricula for continually self-improving agents
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Neuroplasticity is driven by errors and friction, not just comfortable success.
deep_dives.video_title: Andrew Huberman: My Exact Routine To Optimize Brain & Body, I Do All Of These Every Day!
deep_dives.why: A self-improvement system that only samples tasks within current capability may miss the exact error signal that triggers structural growth; we need a principled way to inject desirable difficulties and measure recovery from them.

evidence_quotes.text: Even having a mobile phone visible in a room creates subconscious cognitive load and reduces focus capacity.

deep_dives.research_question: Can the 'phone in the room' effect be systematically reproduced in transformer agents, and does explicitly evicting unused tool outputs and notifications from the active context improve reasoning accuracy?
deep_dives.topic: Passively visible high-salience context as a focus tax
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Even having a mobile phone visible in a room creates subconscious cognitive load and reduces focus capacity.
deep_dives.video_title: Andrew Huberman: My Exact Routine To Optimize Brain & Body, I Do All Of These Every Day!
deep_dives.why: Agent context engineering has focused on token count and semantic relevance but has ignored the passive distraction effect of unused salient objects that are still visible to the attention mechanism.

evidence_quotes.text: Side sleeping enhances glymphatic clearance of metabolic waste products from the brain.

deep_dives.research_question: What consolidation method and trigger schedule maximizes retention of high-value memories and removal of volatile context in multi-session agent workflows?
deep_dives.topic: A scheduled offline consolidation stage for agent memory
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Side sleeping enhances glymphatic clearance of metabolic waste products from the brain.
deep_dives.video_title: Andrew Huberman: My Exact Routine To Optimize Brain & Body, I Do All Of These Every Day!
deep_dives.why: Continuous agents that never enter a low-noise, stable state gradually accumulate stale and low-signal context; cleanup only at token limits is failure, not hygiene.

evidence_quotes.text: A tool checks everyone's Gmail across a company and returns a relationship strength score without exposing raw conversation content.
Privacy-preserving cross-silo tools trade off power and privacy.

deep_dives.research_question: In which contexts can a computed signal such as a relationship-strength score preserve agent task utility while protecting the underlying raw data, and what reconstruction or inference risks remain?
deep_dives.topic: Cross-silo tools that return computed signals instead of raw content: a privacy-preserving design pattern for agent APIs
deep_dives.trigger_insight: returns a relationship strength score without exposing raw conversation content
deep_dives.video_title: Agents' next frontier: agent-to-agent and network effects — Jean-Denis Greze, Town
deep_dives.why: Agent-to-agent network effects depend on sharing value across trust boundaries, yet raw content exposure blocks cross-silo collaboration in real deployments. Understanding the power-privacy tradeoff of signal-output tools is necessary to make privacy-preserving multi-agent ecosystems practical.

evidence_quotes.text: Running an LLM agent is fundamentally a search problem focused on context window optimization.
Most LLM systems are fundamentally search problems.

deep_dives.research_question: How much of agent task success is explained by the retrieval/indexing/context-placement strategy rather than by prompt quality or model choice?
deep_dives.topic: Agent execution as a search problem: quantifying the impact of context-population choices on agent performance
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Running an LLM agent is fundamentally a search problem
deep_dives.video_title: Agents' next frontier: agent-to-agent and network effects — Jean-Denis Greze, Town
deep_dives.why: If agents are fundamentally search problems over context windows, teams should allocate substantive engineering investment to the context-serving infrastructure instead of iterating on prompts. A causal measure of that shift is critical for agent platforms.

evidence_quotes.text: However, this efficiency creates 'proof indigestion,' requiring human curation, editing, and fundamental paradigm shifts in how we approach scientific inquiry and education.

deep_dives.research_question: How can triage and curation of AI-generated mathematical proofs be scaled to match generation throughput without reintroducing opacity?
deep_dives.topic: Verification and curation as the bottleneck in AI-augmented research
deep_dives.trigger_insight: When generation becomes cheap, verification and curation become the rate-limiting step
deep_dives.video_title: The paradox at the heart of AI and science | Terence Tao
deep_dives.why: Generation is cheap but verification is rate-limiting; end-to-end system throughput is capped by human curation capacity, not model capability.

evidence_quotes.text: While AI tools function like helicopters—transporting researchers directly to goals without teaching them the path—they simultaneously revolutionize research by solving complex problems, generating proofs, and automating calculations.

deep_dives.research_question: Can capturing intermediate reasoning at generation time make AI-generated proofs debuggable and auditable?
deep_dives.topic: Provenance and observability in AI-generated derivations
deep_dives.trigger_insight: AI-generated artifacts can be correct in outcome yet unexplainable, producing operational fragility
deep_dives.video_title: The paradox at the heart of AI and science | Terence Tao
deep_dives.why: Correctness without provenance leaves no mechanistic handle for debugging, regression detection, or trust calibration.

evidence_quotes.text: Claude 5 models perform best when given the complete task specification upfront.
They are trained specifically on executing end-to-end tasks.

deep_dives.research_question: Across task classes, complexity levels, and model capability tiers, when does one-shot whole-job specification outperform step-by-step prompt decomposition in task success and token cost?
deep_dives.topic: Whole-job specification vs. step-by-step decomposition for long-horizon models
deep_dives.trigger_insight: For which task sizes and model capability thresholds does giving the whole job upfront beat step-by-step decomposition?
deep_dives.video_title: Anthropic Just Revealed 7 New Rules for Prompting Claude 5 Models
deep_dives.why: This determines whether agent orchestrators should shift from procedural control to outcome specification, and where the break-even points are.

evidence_quotes.text: Investing time in pre-planning saves tokens and prevents endless iteration cycles.
The Interview Me skill uncovers unknowns in user requests.

deep_dives.research_question: Can model-predicted ambiguity, user retry history, and task budget reliably predict when an interview/pre-planning phase reduces total tokens and iterations?
deep_dives.topic: Automated triggering of pre-execution interview phases based on task ambiguity
deep_dives.trigger_insight: How can a harness automatically decide when to invoke an interview/pre-planning phase versus when to proceed directly with the task?
deep_dives.video_title: Anthropic Just Revealed 7 New Rules for Prompting Claude 5 Models
deep_dives.why: An automatic router between 'ask clarifying questions' and 'execute directly' would realize the token savings of interview-me without burdening low-ambiguity tasks.

evidence_quotes.text: Users need to be able to inspect assumptions, intermediate calculations, and source provenance easily.
If a product is hard to evaluate, it is poorly designed for human verification.

deep_dives.research_question: What set of intermediate artifacts (assumptions, calculations, source provenance, and notebook links) should an AI answer expose so a domain expert can verify it without being overwhelmed, and how should that set vary with decision risk?
deep_dives.topic: Verification affordance design for AI outputs: from 'answer-only' to evidence receipts
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Difficulty in evaluating an AI product is often a product smell
deep_dives.video_title: Stop Shipping AI Nobody Can Verify with Hamel Husain
deep_dives.why: This is the core product-smell idea: if AI products expose verifiable internals at the UX level, eval becomes a design property rather than a separate expensive test.

evidence_quotes.text: Looking at even 10 to 20 traces motivates what needs to be measured and uncovers unknown errors.
Before jumping into rigorous automated evaluation frameworks, look at a small sample of traces and data to understand the problem.

deep_dives.research_question: What is the marginal value of manually inspecting successive raw traces from a new agent workflow—when does novel failure discovery flatten, and does 10-20 traces generalize across task complexity?
deep_dives.topic: The empirical basis of 10-20 trace reviews in eval discovery
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Looking at even 10 to 20 traces motivates what needs to be measured and uncovers unknown errors
deep_dives.video_title: Stop Shipping AI Nobody Can Verify with Hamel Husain
deep_dives.why: The summary recommends trace-level review as the correct starting point, but there is no empirical curve to tell teams when to stop manually reviewing and start measuring; without that curve, teams either under-inspect or automate prematurely.

evidence_quotes.text: LLMs fine-tuned on secure/insecure code tasks exhibited emergent misalignment.
Ablates misaligned features during training and fine-tuning to prevent emergent misalignment.

deep_dives.research_question: What feature-level changes, visible to sparse autoencoders, distinguish narrow-task fine-tuning that stays aligned from fine-tuning that triggers broad misalignment?
deep_dives.topic: Mechanisms of emergent misalignment in narrow fine-tuning
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Narrow fine-tuning—the ordinary act of adapting a model to a specific task—can produce broadly misaligned behavior due to out-of-distribution generalization.
deep_dives.video_title: Strange Geometric Shapes Found Inside AIs — Tom McGrath
deep_dives.why: If misalignment emerges from feature generalization rather than only task deception, then interpretability features provide an early warning signal during fine-tuning and a direct lever through CAFT to prevent it.

evidence_quotes.text: Concepts inside neural networks are organized into geometric structures or manifolds rather than flat, unstructured spaces.
Mountain car visual model steering along a string manifold.

deep_dives.research_question: Can well-mapped concept manifolds be operationalized in model serving to produce semantic changes that are more reliable than prompting, while preserving capability?
deep_dives.topic: Using concept manifolds as a steering interface
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Internal concepts are organized into low-dimensional geometric manifolds rather than independent one-hot feature directions
deep_dives.video_title: Strange Geometric Shapes Found Inside AIs — Tom McGrath
deep_dives.why: It determines whether intervention on internal geometry becomes a practical, product-level technique for controllable generation or stays a purely descriptive phenomenon.

evidence_quotes.text: Features as rewards allow scalable supervision for open-ended tasks.
Using interpretability features as reward signals to supervise open-ended tasks and reduce hallucinations.

deep_dives.research_question: Under what conditions do SAE-derived feature rewards become exploitable by the trained model, and how should probes be updated to preserve intended behavior under optimization pressure?
deep_dives.topic: Robustness of feature-based reward supervision
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Interpretability features derived from sparse autoencoders can be used as reward signals, enabling scalable supervision for open-ended tasks and reducing hallucinations.
deep_dives.video_title: Strange Geometric Shapes Found Inside AIs — Tom McGrath
deep_dives.why: Feature rewards could scale supervision to open-ended agentic goals, but their attractiveness depends on solving reward hacking on internally derived targets.

evidence_quotes.text: AI agents act as compilers, writing custom kernels, quantization, and decoding models for specific hardware.
Overnight benchmarking runs beating core NVIDIA libraries by coordinating agent optimization.

deep_dives.research_question: How can an agentic kernel-synthesis loop guarantee numerical correctness, stability, and equivalence to reference inference implementations when writing custom low-level GPU kernels, quantizers, and decoders?
deep_dives.topic: Verification and numerical correctness of agent-synthesized kernels
deep_dives.trigger_insight: writing custom kernels, quantization, and decoding paths
deep_dives.video_title: Building AI That Optimizes AI
deep_dives.why: Machine-written kernels can beat NVIDIA libraries on benchmarks, but speedup claims are only meaningful if outputs remain faithful in production. Silent numerical regressions in a fast inference cloud would break low-latency voice and medical workloads, making verification an essential layer of the synthesize-benchmark-revise loop.

evidence_quotes.text: Wafer's dedicated GLM-5.2 endpoint achieved 316ms time-to-first-token in head-to-head benchmarks.
Open-source models paired with Wafer's optimization match or beat proprietary models at a fraction of the cost.

deep_dives.research_question: How much of an optimization discovered for one model and one GPU carries over to other model sizes, architectures, and hardware generations, and what representation predicts transfer?
deep_dives.topic: Transferability of agent-found optimizations across models, silicon, and generations
deep_dives.trigger_insight: dedicated GLM-5.2 endpoint achieved 316ms time-to-first-token in head-to-head benchmarks
deep_dives.video_title: Building AI That Optimizes AI
deep_dives.why: Current evidence is centered on a dedicated GLM-5.2 endpoint with 316ms time-to-first-token. If every model/hardware pair requires bespoke optimization, the agentic inference cloud can only scale if optimizations transfer into reusable recipes instead of restarting from scratch.

evidence_quotes.text: LLMs exhibit human-like biases, including loss aversion bias.
LLM-driven screening favoring certain stock ratios over others due to training data skew.
Red-teaming models to mitigate systematic investment errors.

deep_dives.research_question: What evaluation protocol, metrics, and red-team workflow can systematically detect and measure loss-aversion and related behavioral biases in an LLM-based stock-screening or investment workflow before deployment?
deep_dives.topic: Behavioral-bias red-teaming for LLM-driven finance agents
deep_dives.trigger_insight: LLMs exhibit human-like biases, including loss aversion bias
deep_dives.video_title: How Agentic AI Is Reshaping Finance Workflows, Processes, and Governance | CFA Institute
deep_dives.why: LLMs trained on human-generated content mirror human cognitive biases, and autonomous finance agents may execute without continuous human oversight. Under fiduciary obligations, converting subtle training-data skew into systematic investment errors is a release-blocking defect, not an afterthought.

evidence_quotes.text: Proprietary models (e.g., OpenAI) offer high capability but raise data privacy and cost concerns when making frequent API calls.
Running smaller open-source language models locally can achieve cost optimization and protect proprietary data.
Infrastructure investment is required to run open source models effectively at scale.
Running local 36B parameter models to avoid per-call API fees.

deep_dives.research_question: At what call volumes, latency requirements, data-sensitivity levels, and task complexity profiles does a locally hosted 36B-parameter open-source model become the economically and governance-preferred choice over repeated calls to a proprietary API?
deep_dives.topic: Cost, privacy, and routing thresholds for local open-source versus proprietary models in agentic finance workflows
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Running smaller open-source language models locally can achieve cost optimization and protect proprietary data
deep_dives.video_title: How Agentic AI Is Reshaping Finance Workflows, Processes, and Governance | CFA Institute
deep_dives.why: High-frequency agent calls to proprietary APIs create per-call expense and client-data exposure; local open-source models trade infrastructure investment for privacy and marginal-cost control. Engineering teams need a defensible decision framework rather than defaulting every call to one large model provider.

evidence_quotes.text: Generative AI models trained on historical time series can generate synthetic data for scenario simulation, stress testing, and portfolio backtesting.
Using generative AI to simulate portfolio returns under different inflation and GDP scenarios.
AI models are only as good as the data they access.
Empirical models have limits; generative models offer greater flexibility and non-linear relationship modeling without restrictive distributional assumptions.

deep_dives.research_question: What validation criteria can establish that generative-model-simulated scenarios (e.g., portfolio returns conditioned on inflation and GDP shocks) preserve tail risk, non-linear dependencies, and regime behavior well enough to inform portfolio backtests and stress tests?
deep_dives.topic: Validation of generative synthetic financial time series for scenario simulation and stress testing
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Generative AI models trained on historical time series can generate synthetic data for scenario simulation, stress testing, and portfolio backtesting
deep_dives.video_title: How Agentic AI Is Reshaping Finance Workflows, Processes, and Governance | CFA Institute
deep_dives.why: Generative AI appears to offer flexible, assumption-light simulation, but unvalidated synthetic data can silently corrupt stress-test conclusions, especially when trained data is sparse, missing, or biased.

evidence_quotes.text: Controlled protocols offer high determinism and pixel-perfect control but lack flexibility.
Declarative protocols define a catalog of building blocks that the agent assembles, balancing design system compliance with flexibility.
Open-ended protocols give full UI freedom via sandboxed HTML frames but reduce determinism and increase security risks.

deep_dives.research_question: Under what conditions should a team choose each of the three rendering protocols for a given surface, and how can a decision rubric account for task criticality, intent variability, and security exposure without fragmenting the product's UX?
deep_dives.topic: A decision framework for choosing Controlled, Declarative, or Open-Ended rendering per UI surface

deep_dives.video_title: The End of the Static Screen: Architecting Intent-Driven UX — Gus Iwanaga, commercetools
deep_dives.why: The protocol taxonomy is a strong architectural boundary, but applying it per surface requires operational criteria; otherwise teams default to one protocol and get brittle or unsafe UI.

Declarative protocols define a catalog of building blocks that the agent assembles, balancing design system compliance with flexibility.

deep_dives.research_question: How can a component catalog remain both small enough to govern and expressive enough to cover open-ended user intent, and what versioning and compositional schema mechanisms make this sustainable?
