deep_dives.why: Engineering leaders are using reported agentic-tool productivity gains to freeze hiring and reallocate workforces. A false positive creates capacity and skill gaps; a false negative deprioritizes a structural efficiency shift.

evidence_quotes.text: Repeating formulas and ideas from past victories without adapting to new opponents and circumstances leads to defeat.
Miyamoto Musashi varying his approach for every opponent; military commanders failing when relying on outdated playbooks.

deep_dives.research_question: Under what measurable environmental-shift conditions does injecting retrieved successful past trajectories into an agent's context reduce task performance versus per-episode re-derivation, and what online detector can gate the injection?
deep_dives.topic: Shift-gated trajectory memory: when does retrieving past victories become the cause of defeat?
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Do not fight the last war
deep_dives.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk
deep_dives.why: Default agent-memory design treats top-k successful trajectories as canonical exemplars. Pass-1 asserts this is a failure mode ('do not fight the last war') rather than a shortcut, so the memory pipeline needs a validation gate before it injects a prior playbook — otherwise the agent confidently applies stale formulas exactly when the environment has shifted and reliability matters most.

evidence_quotes.text: Tactics alone leads to 'tactical hell' where one is constantly reacting and losing control.
Grand strategy is a stairway to elevate oneself above stressful situations to get perspective on the entire battlefield.

deep_dives.research_question: Does an explicit higher-abstraction layer that consumes a compressed situation model and rewrites the reactive layer's goals outperform a single monolithic loop with equal reasoning strength per step?
deep_dives.topic: Two-tier control: a reactive controller plus an elevation layer that rewrites its objectives
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Tactics alone leads to 'tactical hell'
deep_dives.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk
deep_dives.why: If tactical hell is an architecture problem and not an intelligence problem, then improving per-step reasoning cannot fix it. The engineering consequence is a defined interface at the tier boundary: what state crosses upward, how often goals are rewritten, and where control cost is paid. This is directly testable by holding the policy fixed and only varying the presence of the elevation layer.

evidence_quotes.text: The Tet Offensive as a tactical defeat for the Viet Cong that became a strategic victory through cultural and political impact on the US.
Strategy requires understanding the culture and social environment of the opponent.

deep_dives.research_question: How do you construct and independently validate a governing-objective metric when the operative tactical metric is anti-correlated with it, and does optimizing the operative metric alone invert true performance?
deep_dives.topic: Metric hierarchies and proxy inversion: scoring at the governing-objective level
deep_dives.trigger_insight: tactical defeat that became a strategic victory
deep_dives.video_title: Applying Military Strategy in Life - Microsoft Talk
deep_dives.why: The Tet Offensive case establishes that a tactical loss can be a strategic victory, which means any eval harness scoring only local success signals cannot safely drive self-improvement, routing, or critique loops. This forces a concrete artifact: an explicit hierarchy of metrics with a stated mapping to the governing objective, plus an independent strategic scorer.

evidence_quotes.text: Deciding what is inside or outside a system is subjective and impacts analysis.
Be mindful of subjectivity and assumptions when drawing system boundaries.
Boundaries define limits or edges of a system, separating what is included and excluded.

deep_dives.research_question: Can boundary judgments be encoded as an explicit, versioned, machine-checkable artifact (included tools, data, signals, memory scope, and excluded items with rationale) such that a scope diff mechanically triggers re-evaluation of the affected eval classes?
deep_dives.topic: Scope manifests as versioned boundary judgments for AI systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: what is placed inside versus outside the system is a subjective judgment
deep_dives.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023
deep_dives.why: Boundary choice is currently an accident of implementation defaults (whatever context, tools, or data happened to be wired in), which silently excludes the factors most likely to explain failures. If scope can be represented, diffed, and tied to eval suites, then an exclusion becomes a reviewable assumption with change control instead of an invisible blind spot.

evidence_quotes.text: Helps understand how complex systems function and how they can be made more effective through five key functions.

Goal setting
  - Resource allocation
  - Decision making
  - Monitoring
  - Coordination

deep_dives.research_question: Does decomposing an agent runtime into five independently inspectable functions (goal setting, resource allocation, decision making, monitoring, coordination) improve drift detection and conflict reconciliation relative to a single decision loop that folds them together?
deep_dives.topic: Separating monitoring and coordination from the decision path
deep_dives.trigger_insight: five separable functions
deep_dives.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023
deep_dives.why: Runtimes that fold monitoring into the decision path lose the ability to detect their own drift, and runtimes that fold coordination into goal setting lose the ability to reconcile conflicting subagents. Naming the five functions as separate components yields a concrete checklist of what must be independently testable and replaceable.

evidence_quotes.text: Behaviors arise from interactions among system parts rather than individual parts alone.
Focus on improving interactions and relationships within systems to alter outcomes.

deep_dives.research_question: If emergent behavior originates in interactions rather than components, do measurable properties of interactions (handoff contracts, message schemas, retry/return paths, routing topology) correlate with task failures better than per-component scores?
deep_dives.topic: Interaction-level telemetry as a replacement for component-level scoring
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Emergent behavior is attributed to interactions among components rather than to the components themselves
deep_dives.video_title: The basics of systems thinking 2023
deep_dives.why: Most agent debugging targets the individual component: swap the model, rewrite the prompt, tune a tool. If behavior is generated at the interaction layer, component-level fixes cannot be reliably effective, and the leverage sits in routing, handoff contracts, and message schemas. This predicts that teams instrumenting interactions debug faster than teams instrumenting components.

evidence_quotes.text: Complex systems are defined by interactions between components, not the components themselves.
Studying a single ant vs an ant colony

deep_dives.research_question: When a multi-agent system fails, how much of the failure variance is attributable to interaction topology, message contracts, and shared-context dynamics versus individual agent capability?
deep_dives.topic: Interaction-first architecture for agentic systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Complex systems are defined by interactions between components, not the components themselves
deep_dives.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
deep_dives.why: Agentic systems are complex systems; if interactions dominate behaviour, isolated prompt/model testing cannot catch systemic failures, and engineering investment should shift to interaction protocols, feedback loops, and population-level tests.

evidence_quotes.text: Stable-looking systems can collapse rapidly when positive feedback loops push them to the edge of chaos.
Small causes can trigger massive global impacts when systems reach critical points.

deep_dives.research_question: Which measurable telemetry signals—feedback-loop strength, rate of change, variance, lag-1 autocorrelation—give warning before an agent system crosses a tipping point, and can dampers be placed before collapse occurs?
deep_dives.topic: Early-warning signals for feedback-driven collapse in multi-agent workloads
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Stable-looking systems can collapse rapidly when positive feedback loops push them to the edge of chaos
deep_dives.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
deep_dives.why: Stable-looking systems with positive feedback can collapse suddenly, and conventional level metrics like latency or error rate may not signal an approaching phase transition.

evidence_quotes.text: Macro-level outcomes can be far more extreme than micro-level intentions due to emergent interactions.
Emergence of full racial segregation from mild individual preferences.

deep_dives.research_question: At what preference thresholds, network structures, and feedback strengths do mild local agent preferences become population-level monoculture, lock-in, or cascading failure, and what guardrails can be introduced pre-deployment?
deep_dives.topic: Mild local preferences and emergent population pathologies in multi-agent systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Macro-level outcomes can be far more extreme than micro-level intentions due to emergent interactions.
deep_dives.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
deep_dives.why: Local design decisions look safe individually, but emergence decouples macro outcomes from micro intentions; safety must therefore be validated at population level rather than by checking individual agent rules.

evidence_quotes.text: Machine learning acts as a black box that yields prediction without understanding.
Agent-based modelling provides understanding of emergent behavior without high predictive accuracy.

deep_dives.research_question: How should an engineering team combine black-box machine-learning prediction with agent-based mechanistic modelling so that forecasting and root-cause explanation are both first-class capabilities?
deep_dives.topic: Hybrid predictive-mechanistic evaluation for agent systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Machine learning acts as a black box that yields prediction without understanding
deep_dives.video_title: Complex Systems Thinking – How to change the way we think about problem solving
deep_dives.why: LLM evals and trace analytics give prediction without understanding while ABMs give understanding without high predictive accuracy; relying on a single all-purpose evaluation sacrifices one of these capabilities.

evidence_quotes.text: Counting negatives in a loop determines loop polarity (odd = balancing, even = reinforcing).
Reinforcing loops amplify change; balancing loops seek goals or balance.

deep_dives.research_question: How can LLM-generated causal graphs or causal discovery methods reliably infer reinforcing vs. balancing loop polarity from agent action/observation traces?
deep_dives.topic: Automated feedback loop polarity detection in agentic systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Counting negatives in a loop determines loop polarity
deep_dives.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
deep_dives.why: Feedback loop polarity predicts whether an interaction will amplify or stabilize, enabling lightweight static analysis of agent interaction graphs before simulation.

evidence_quotes.text: A stock is anything that accumulates over time and has memory.
To change a stock, you must alter inflows or outflows.

deep_dives.research_question: What are optimal inflow and outflow policies for context/memory as a stock in agents with bounded context windows?
deep_dives.topic: Stock-flow memory management for long-horizon agents
deep_dives.trigger_insight: stocks accumulate over time and have memory
deep_dives.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
deep_dives.why: Context behaves as a stock with memory; managing it with explicit inflow and outflow policies prevents uncontrolled growth and preserves relevant information.

evidence_quotes.text: Failing to account for delays leads to overshooting and policy resistance.
Systems feature tight coupling and time delays between decisions and system state changes, leading to unintended consequences.

deep_dives.research_question: How can agents measure action-effect delays and adapt their control rate to avoid overshooting and oscillation?
deep_dives.topic: Delay-aware control for stable agent loops
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Failing to account for delays leads to overshooting and policy resistance
deep_dives.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
deep_dives.why: Ignoring delays between decisions and observable state changes causes overcorrection, wasted tool calls, and policy resistance in autonomous agents.

evidence_quotes.text: Structure generates behavior.
Dynamics emerge from the interaction of physics, information availability, and decision rules.

deep_dives.research_question: What methods can systematically trace persistent agent failures back to structural causes such as information availability, decision rules, and incentives?
deep_dives.topic: Structural debugging: tracing agent failures to architecture rather than the model
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Structure generates behavior
deep_dives.video_title: System Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World
deep_dives.why: The fundamental attribution error in AI debugging blames the model when persistent failures are symptoms of surrounding structure, so durable fixes require structural analysis.

evidence_quotes.text: Continuous flow approximation works extremely well in queuing applications and reduces errors compared to measurement uncertainty.
Choosing continuous vs discrete depends entirely on the purpose of the model.

deep_dives.research_question: At what arrival-rate / queue-length regime does an aggregate continuous approximation produce lower end-to-end decision error than a per-event discrete representation of the same system?
deep_dives.topic: Crossover point between continuous and discrete representation for decision-making
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Continuous flow approximation works extremely well in queuing applications
deep_dives.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski
deep_dives.why: Agent runtimes default to fine-grained per-event or per-token traces on the assumption that fidelity equals accuracy. If aggregate abstraction measurably lowers decision error because it filters measurement noise, then observability granularity becomes a tunable evaluation parameter with direct cost and reliability consequences rather than a fixed design default.

evidence_quotes.text: Building a model using an outside-in approach helps distinguish exogenous constants from endogenous variables and enforce units.
Enables unit inheritance, model transparency, and clear identification of policy variables.

deep_dives.research_question: Does propagating declared types/units structurally through a dependency graph (constants to stocks to auxiliaries) catch more integration defects than validating types at each tool-call boundary?
deep_dives.topic: Structural unit/type inheritance as an alternative to boundary validation in agent tool orchestration
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Building a model using an outside-in approach helps distinguish exogenous constants from endogenous variables
deep_dives.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics Modeling | Seminar Series | Len Malczynski
deep_dives.why: Most agent systems validate structured output at the boundary of every call, treating correctness as a per-hop check. Inheritance makes correctness a construction-time property of the graph, converting silent integration errors into build-time failures and removing an entire review step. The cost is that the vocabulary must be committed before any logic is written.

evidence_quotes.text: There are nine holistic thinking perspectives analogous to the blind men and the elephant parable.
External perspectives cover big picture and operational views.
Internal perspectives cover functional and structural views (analysis).
Progressive perspectives cover generic, continuum, and temporal views.

deep_dives.research_question: Can the nine Holistic Thinking Perspectives (big picture, operational, functional, structural, generic, continuum, temporal, quantitative, scientific) be encoded as a detection-and-scoring rubric that a model can apply to a system or agent design artifact, and does multi-perspective coverage catch defects that single-perspective review misses?
deep_dives.topic: Operationalizing the nine Holistic Thinking Perspectives as an automated design-review rubric
deep_dives.trigger_insight: There are nine holistic thinking perspectives analogous to the blind men and the elephant parable.
deep_dives.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering
deep_dives.why: A fixed enumerated perspective set turns a vague instruction ('think holistically') into a countable coverage check. If it works, it becomes a reusable review gate for architecture docs, tool schemas, and agent specifications, and it supplies a concrete explanation for why single-view reviews pass designs that later fail.

evidence_quotes.text: Optimizing subsystems independently does not lead to a system optimum; you must optimize the system as a whole.

deep_dives.research_question: In a decomposed agent or software pipeline, what mechanism makes component metrics derive from a single system-level objective, and does per-component optimization measurably degrade end-to-end outcomes compared with whole-system objective optimization?
deep_dives.topic: Propagating a whole-system objective down to independently tunable components
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Optimizing subsystems independently does not lead to a system optimum
deep_dives.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering
deep_dives.why: This is the highest-leverage architectural consequence in the set: it converts 'per-agent success metrics' from an assumed good into a suspected failure mode, and it demands instrumentation that ties component behavior to end-to-end outcomes rather than to local scores.

evidence_quotes.text: George follows standards meticulously but fails because he cannot understand what the customer really wants.
Early stages of problem formulation and conceptualization are missing from standards.
Standards like DoD Directive 5000 and EIA-632 focus on managing the process (management of systems engineering) rather than doing systems engineering.

deep_dives.research_question: Can under-specified or misunderstood user intent be detected before solution work begins, and does inserting an explicit, scored formulation stage reduce rework relative to process-only workflows?
deep_dives.topic: Making intent elicitation and problem formulation a measured stage, not an assumed one
deep_dives.trigger_insight: George follows standards meticulously but fails because he cannot understand what the customer really wants.
deep_dives.video_title: Systems thinking as it applies to systems engineering
deep_dives.why: Names a concrete failure mode that transfers directly to agent systems that pass step-by-step workflow checks yet miss user intent. If formulation is unmeasured, evaluation harnesses will certify process-compliant failures; the fix is a first-class gate plus an intent-alignment score.

evidence_quotes.text: systemic properties only appear at the system level
Reductionism studies objects in isolation by taking them apart from the bottom up

deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice

evidence_quotes.text: Identified five necessary functions: System 5 (policy/identity), System 4 (intelligence/environment), System 3 (control/overview), System 2 (stability/coordination), and System 1 (sub-systems/operations).
Successful systems must be able to adapt and survive over time.

deep_dives.topic: Viable System Model as a diagnostic audit for agent architectures
deep_dives.trigger_insight: five necessary functions: System 5 (policy/identity), System 4 (intelligence/environment), System 3 (control/overview), System 2 (stability/coordination), and System 1 (sub-systems/operations)
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice
deep_dives.why: Agent systems that fuse execution, coordination, auditing, environment scanning, and policy into a single loop may be unable to adapt to environmental changes; VSM gives a grounded set of functions to inspect.

evidence_quotes.text: How we draw the line between the system and the environment is a matter of judgement.

deep_dives.research_question: How should decisions about what an agent can see, remember, and do be formalized so that boundary exclusions become explicit, contestable, and revisable by affected stakeholders?
deep_dives.topic: Boundary judgement governance for agent context and tooling
deep_dives.trigger_insight: How we draw the line between the system and the environment is a matter of judgement.
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking in Practice
deep_dives.why: Agent context, memory, tool access, and permitted scope are boundary judgements that encode values and determine whose interests count; leaving them implicit bakes those choices in without discussion.

evidence_quotes.text: Systems thinking expands binary answers into four possibilities: yes, no, it depends, and don't know/care.
Systems thinking recognizes a continuum of solutions: optimal, acceptable, and unacceptable.

deep_dives.research_question: Does a four-valued output contract (yes/no/it depends/don't know) reduce false commitments on ambiguous inputs compared to binary or probability-threshold contracts?
deep_dives.topic: Four-valued answer schemas for ambiguous agent outputs
deep_dives.trigger_insight: four-valued answer schema (yes / no / it depends / don't know)
deep_dives.video_title: Why you should be using systems thinking to solve problems

evidence_quotes.text: Acronym for Stay calm, Think, Ask questions and analyze answers, Listen, Listen.
Prevents premature knee-jerk reactions and improves information gathering.

evidence_quotes.text: Essential properties of any system derive from how its parts interact, not how they act separately.
When the whole is disassembled, it loses its essential properties, as do all of its parts.
A system is a whole that cannot be divided into independent parts.

deep_dives.research_question: If the essential properties of an agentic system live in the interactions between agents, tools, memory and router, can an evaluation harness that ablates interfaces rather than components detect emergent regressions that component-level benchmarks miss?
deep_dives.topic: Interaction-level evaluation harnesses for agentic systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Essential properties of any system derive from how its parts interact, not how they act separately.
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff
deep_dives.why: Component benchmarks implicitly assume parts act independently, which is exactly the assumption systems thinking denies; teams may be shipping on green dashboards while end-to-end behavior degrades, so the evaluation unit itself must be re-specified.

evidence_quotes.text: Dissolution involves redesigning the system so that the problem no longer exists, which requires design rather than mere analysis.
The elevator waiting time problem in office buildings resolved by adding mirrors in lobbies so people spend time looking at each other rather than complaining about elevator speed.

deep_dives.research_question: What decision criteria (failure recurrence rate, redesign cost, structural eliminability) reliably predict that a repeated agent failure class should be dissolved through task/interface redesign rather than patched at the model or prompt layer?
deep_dives.topic: Dissolution triage: when to redesign the system instead of fixing it
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Dissolution involves redesigning the system so that the problem no longer exists
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff
deep_dives.why: Most production firefighting is resolution or solution; a triage rubric would route recurring, structurally-eliminable failures to the architecture and product-interface layers where dissolution actually happens, instead of burning model-layer effort on symptom suppression.

evidence_quotes.text: When a system is operating as well as possible, none of its parts may be operating as well as possible.
Divide and conquer is fundamentally false when applied to systems because the whole is the product of the interaction of its parts.

deep_dives.research_question: Can a multi-agent pipeline that deliberately tolerates individually suboptimal agents (lower per-agent accuracy, higher per-agent latency) outperform a pipeline where each agent is tuned to its own local optimum, on an end-to-end task metric?
deep_dives.topic: System-level objective functions versus per-component optimization
deep_dives.trigger_insight: When a system is operating as well as possible, none of its parts may be operating as well as possible.
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking, Learning, and Problem Solving by Russell L. Ackoff
deep_dives.why: Per-agent accuracy, per-tool precision and per-retriever recall are the default targets in agent engineering; if the global optimum requires suboptimal parts, then KPI design, dashboards and reward signals must move to the interaction level and teams must accept visible component 'regressions'.

evidence_quotes.text: School is about performing for someone else's approval, not about learning.
The prevailing system of management and schooling is not about learning; it's about control.

deep_dives.research_question: Do proxy performance metrics in agent development necessarily displace genuine capability acquisition, and can diagnostic feedback prevent divergence between proxy score and held-out competence?

deep_dives.trigger_insight: described as control rather than learning
deep_dives.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline
deep_dives.why: If proxy metrics crowd out learning, benchmark-dominated development will produce compliant but incompetent agents. Understanding this trade-off is central to building reliable AI.

evidence_quotes.text: Culture is the assumptions we cannot see.
If you want to transform institutions, you must examine the deep, pervasive assumptions underlying the industrial age.

deep_dives.research_question: How can implicit assumptions embedded in prompts, tool schemas, and reward rubrics be surfaced, represented, and audited in agentic systems, and does making them explicit change system behavior?
deep_dives.topic: Making implicit priors explicit in agentic systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Culture is defined as the assumptions members cannot see
deep_dives.video_title: Peter Senge, The Fifth Discipline
deep_dives.why: Implicit priors govern agent behavior but are not inspectable artifacts, making behavioral change unreliable. Explicit representation is a prerequisite for auditing and debugging.

evidence_quotes.text: Warehouses and inventory are bad because they hide defects and cost money.
NeXT built a true JIT (Just-In-Time) factory in Fremont, California with no warehouse.

deep_dives.research_question: How does the lag between generating an artifact and detecting its defects affect defect escape rate in AI pipelines, and what is the minimum achievable latency before throughput degrades?
deep_dives.topic: Artifact-to-detection latency as a reliability mechanism
deep_dives.trigger_insight: eliminating the lag between producing an artifact and detecting that it is broken
deep_dives.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech
deep_dives.why: Any buffer between generation and evaluation—batched evals, review queues, cached outputs—conceals failures until they are expensive to attribute and fix. Minimizing this lag is a reliability mechanism, not just an ops nicety.

evidence_quotes.text: By providing reusable object-oriented software libraries, NeXT enabled developers to write 80% fewer lines of code.
NextStep allows building apps 5 to 10 times faster by reusing existing objects.

deep_dives.research_question: Can 'fraction of implementation not authored by the application builder' be operationalized as a stable, comparable benchmark across agent frameworks and tool platforms?
deep_dives.topic: Authored surface area as a platform metric
deep_dives.trigger_insight: the leverage is in the number of components not rewritten
deep_dives.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech
deep_dives.why: It provides a concrete, measurable metric for platform leverage: the proportion of implementation a builder avoids writing, rather than how pleasant the authoring experience is. Frameworks that maximize reuse of pre-built components deliver step-change speedups.

evidence_quotes.text: Hardware churns every 18 months, making sustainable competitive advantage from hardware nearly impossible.
Software takes much longer for competitors to catch up with (4 to 5 years).

deep_dives.research_question: Does investment in system layers with longer replication lag (e.g., data, evaluation harnesses, workflow integration) produce more durable competitive advantage than investment in fast-churning layers (e.g., models, hardware)?
deep_dives.topic: Replication lag as moat selection criterion
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Advantage is a function of time-to-copy
deep_dives.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech
deep_dives.why: It offers a principled selection criterion for what to build versus buy and where to invest engineering effort, by treating replication lag as the primary determinant of defensibility.

evidence_quotes.text: Companies across the board spend about 2 percent of revenues on IT regardless of success.
Successful companies spend most of their IT budget on operational productivity and custom applications.
New products require custom operational apps; without an app, you don't have a product.

deep_dives.research_question: Does the operational-versus-management IT spending split predict organizational success in the AI era, and can it guide where AI investments create measurable value?
deep_dives.topic: Operational vs. management productivity in AI spending
deep_dives.trigger_insight: successful companies concentrate spend on operational productivity
deep_dives.video_title: Steve Jobs MIT 1992: Steve Jobs Talk, Steve Jobs Speech
deep_dives.why: It provides a prior for where AI adoption creates value: embedded workflow-specific systems that execute core operations, versus general-purpose assistant tooling aimed at knowledge-worker convenience.

evidence_quotes.text: When you take a system apart, it loses its essential properties (e.g., an automobile disassembled is not an automobile).
Essential properties of a system are properties of the whole which none of its parts have.

deep_dives.research_question: Can a capability exhibited by an assembled agent system in its operating environment be shown to be absent or degraded when the same system is evaluated as decomposed components?
deep_dives.topic: Non-decomposable whole-system evaluation boundaries
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Essential properties of a system are properties of the whole which none of its parts have
deep_dives.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking
deep_dives.why: Most agent platforms are validated per-component (prompt tests, tool unit tests, single-model evals). If the properties that matter only exist at the whole-system level, part-level metrics are not estimates of capability but upper bounds, and the harness is structurally blind to the dominant failure modes.

evidence_quotes.text: Analysis reveals structure and how a system works; synthesis reveals why it works the way it does.
Systems thinking is the fusion of analysis and synthesis depending on whether the objective is knowledge or understanding.

deep_dives.research_question: Do different choices of containing-system boundary (objective, stakeholder, environment) change measured system performance and failure attribution on the same agent system?
deep_dives.topic: Boundary selection for synthesis: choosing the containing system
deep_dives.trigger_insight: how do you choose the containing system for a given engineering problem
deep_dives.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking
deep_dives.why: Synthesis is defined philosophically but has no procedure. Without boundary-selection heuristics, teams default to structural decomposition, and recurring failures get patched locally because the explanatory layer that would locate the failure in a containing objective is missing.

evidence_quotes.text: Social systems (corporations, hospitals) are made of purposeful parts (people) with their own wills
Organisms have purposes of their own (survival and growth), whereas machines have functions to serve external purposes.

deep_dives.research_question: For multi-agent and multi-model systems, does an explicit objective-level coordination mechanism outperform instruction-dispatch plus retries on tasks where components have partially conflicting objectives?
deep_dives.topic: Functional vs purposeful components and objective-level coordination
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Social systems (corporations, hospitals) are made of purposeful parts (people) with their own wills
deep_dives.video_title: Russell L Ackoff From Mechanistic to Systemic thinking
deep_dives.why: It relocates control logic. If components are purposeful rather than functional, command-and-control orchestration is the wrong abstraction, and a new runtime concern appears: representing component objectives and resolving conflicts between them.

evidence_quotes.text: Overshoot-collapse occurs when carrying capacity is erodable and there is a response delay.
Delayed response occurs with non-erodable carrying capacity and response delay, leading to oscillations.
Sigmoid growth occurs with immediate, accurate response or natural growth saturation short of carrying capacity.

deep_dives.research_question: Can an agentic runtime estimate, at run time, both the response delay and the erodability of each of its resource loops (context budget, provider quota, vector store quality, human review bandwidth) and derive the correct control policy from that classification alone?
deep_dives.topic: Run-time regime classification of agent resource loops (delay × erodability)
deep_dives.trigger_insight: whether the limit (carrying capacity) is erodable, and whether the corrective feedback responds with delay
deep_dives.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse
deep_dives.why: The pass-1 taxonomy is a design-time diagnostic applied by a human analyst; making it an online controller requires measurable proxies for delay (response-time lag, propagation lag) and erodability (does quality/availability return to baseline after load reduction), plus a decision rule that maps the two booleans onto cap-and-margin versus throttle-and-damp behavior. Without this, every operator re-derives the classification by intuition and mis-tunes collapse-mode resources as if they oscillated.

evidence_quotes.text: Exponential growth requires a dominating positive feedback loop.
When predators were removed, the positive feedback loop of deer birth rate dominated, leading to exponential growth.

deep_dives.research_question: Can a production-trace replay harness that removes a proposed balancing loop (critic, verifier, throttle, human approval) detect a qualitative behavior-mode change — oscillation versus collapse versus runway growth — rather than only a throughput delta?
deep_dives.topic: Counterfactual loop-removal testing before shipping a guardrail change
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Removing a single balancing (negative) feedback loop converts a stable equilibrium into a dominating positive feedback loop
deep_dives.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse
deep_dives.why: Loop removal is currently justified by latency and cost savings and assumed to degrade gracefully; the pass-1 mechanism claim says it changes the qualitative behavior mode. A replay harness that classifies the counterfactual run's mode gives a shipping gate for guardrail deletions, and requires a mode taxonomy plus a statistical test that distinguishes noisy throughput change from mode change.

evidence_quotes.text: Overshoot-collapse occurs when carrying capacity is erodable and there is a response delay.
turning temporary overshoot into permanent collapse

deep_dives.research_question: Which resource limits in an agent platform can be converted into genuinely non-erodable limits (enforced hard caps, pre-reserved quotas, immutable snapshots) so that overshoot becomes damped oscillation instead of collapse, and what is the cost of that conversion per resource class?
deep_dives.topic: Engineering erodability away: which agent resources can be made non-erodable
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Which resource limits in an agent platform can be made genuinely non-erodable
deep_dives.video_title: Systems: Overshoot and Collapse
deep_dives.why: The pass-1 material treats erodability as a property of the modeled system, not an engineering choice; if erodability can be designed away even partially, that is the highest-leverage intervention available, because it removes the collapse mode entirely rather than mitigating its symptoms. The deliverable is a comparison of enforcement mechanisms per resource class with measured recovery-curve behavior after load reduction.

deep_dives.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series

evidence_quotes.text: Every system has only two types of concepts: levels (accumulations) and rates (policies governing actions).
Level equations are integrations (accounting statements of backlog plus incoming orders minus production).

deep_dives.research_question: Can agent context/memory be formalized as level equations and agent policies as rate equations, such that automated validators (analogous to dimensional consistency) can be run over an agent pipeline before deployment?
deep_dives.topic: Level/Rate Formalization for Agent Runtimes
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Can agent context/memory be formalized as level equations
deep_dives.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester
deep_dives.why: The summary asserts levels and rates as the only two system concepts and mentions dimensional consistency as terminology, but gives no method for constructing or validating such models for software agents. Without this, agent state and policy remain entangled and unauditable.

deep_dives.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series

evidence_quotes.text: Large order backlogs feel comfortable initially, but excessive delivery delays erode sales effectiveness and destroy market share.
Companies often blame competitors or banks for low profits when problems are self-induced by internal delivery delays and pricing policies.

deep_dives.research_question: What delay magnitude inside an agent feedback loop begins to degrade the policy's own effectiveness, and is there a measurable 'self-induced stagnation' signature in task success or adoption?
deep_dives.topic: Delay Thresholds and Self-Induced Stagnation in Agent Loops
deep_dives.trigger_insight: What delay magnitude inside an agent feedback loop begins to degrade
deep_dives.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester
deep_dives.why: The summary states the delay-to-effectiveness-erosion mechanism qualitatively via the backlog example but offers no threshold or measurement of when it becomes destructive. For agent systems, queue depth is treated as a throughput metric, not a stability parameter.

deep_dives.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series

evidence_quotes.text: When organizations fail to meet absolute goals, pressure forces goals downward to match reality, creating an eroding spiral.
Absolute goals versus effective (floating) goals governed by traditions and past performance.

deep_dives.research_question: Does explicitly separating immutable absolute goals from floating operating targets reduce goal erosion and reward drift in long-horizon agent optimization?
deep_dives.topic: Two-Tier Goal Structures to Prevent Reward Drift
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Does explicitly separating immutable absolute goals from floating operating targets
deep_dives.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester
deep_dives.why: The eroding-goal structure is described as an observed organizational dynamic, but the summary provides no experiment on preventing or reversing it in software optimizers. If confirmed, it prescribes a concrete architectural pattern for autonomous systems.

deep_dives.channel: James R. Killian, Jr. Lecture Series

evidence_quotes.text: Most cocktail party and congressional conversations assume an open-loop view where actions solve problems directly.
The real world is a continuous, circular, closed-loop feedback system with no beginning and no end.

deep_dives.research_question: Do LLM agents exhibit a default open-loop assumption bias — acting as if an action produced the intended result without verifying state change — and can that be detected as a distinct failure class?
deep_dives.topic: Open-Loop Bias in LLM Agents
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Do LLM agents exhibit a default open-loop assumption bias
deep_dives.video_title: The Common Foundation Underlying Physical and Social Systems - Jay W. Forrester
deep_dives.why: The summary argues open-loop thinking dominates human decision-making but does not address model behavior; nothing in the source establishes whether this bias transfers to agent harnesses. If it does, mandatory post-action state verification becomes a structural requirement.

evidence_quotes.text: Dissolution redesigns the system so that the problem no longer exists.
Introduces design as a higher-order problem-handling methodology than mere optimization or scientific problem-solving.

deep_dives.research_question: Can dissolution-class fixes be generated by a systematic search over task, environment, and interface redesigns, and do they outperform solving-class fixes on recurrence rate and total cost?
deep_dives.topic: Operationalizing Dissolution as a Search Process
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Can dissolution be operationalized as an explicit search process over task, environment, and interface redesigns rather than an act of creative insight?
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff
deep_dives.why: Agent systems overwhelmingly attack failures inside the existing loop. If dissolution can be operationalized, reliability engineering shifts from optimizing solutions to redesigning systems, potentially eliminating failure classes rather than reducing their frequency.

evidence_quotes.text: None of the parts has an independent effect on the whole.
Improving the performance of parts taken separately does not necessarily improve the whole.
When a system operates as well as possible, none of its parts may be operating as well as possible.

deep_dives.research_question: Does optimizing individual agents or tools to their own benchmarks reliably reduce end-to-end task success, and can the degradation be predicted from measured coupling strength?
deep_dives.topic: Measuring End-to-End Degradation from Per-Component Optimization
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Does per-component optimization reliably degrade end-to-end performance in multi-agent or tool-chain systems
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking Speech by Dr. Russell Ackoff
deep_dives.why: Standard agent-engineering practice benchmarks and tunes each component to local best-in-class performance, but if this actively harms system-level outcomes, evaluation budgets and design principles must shift to interaction surfaces and end-to-end traces.

evidence_quotes.text: Distinctions (Identity-Other)
Systems (Part-Whole)
Relationships (Action-Reaction)
Perspectives (Point-View)
All mental models and knowledge are built from four fundamental patterns (DSRP).

deep_dives.research_question: If every structuring step must emit both the figure and its ground (Identity-Other, Part-Whole, Action-Reaction, Point-View), does enforcement of the complement field improve agent problem-solving accuracy and error detection versus salient-only representation?
deep_dives.topic: DSRP as a machine-checkable schema with enforced complements
deep_dives.trigger_insight: DSRP defines four named structural operators, each defined as a complementary pair

evidence_quotes.text: Lots of information makes us informed, but lots of thinking makes us smart.
Information alone isn't enough to solve problems; we need thinking to build meaning from information.

deep_dives.research_question: Holding task type constant, does added retrieved information without added structuring improve decision quality above baseline, and can structuring depth be measured independently of context volume?
deep_dives.topic: Structuring transform versus information volume in agent context
deep_dives.trigger_insight: The film separates information (raw input, storage) from thinking (the operation that builds meaning)
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab
deep_dives.why: Challenges the dominant scaling assumption in context engineering and implies that representation-quality evaluation should be separated from retrieval recall evaluation, since a system can be information-rich and structurally poor.

evidence_quotes.text: Mental models determine how we feel and how we act.
It's your mental model that makes the difference.
Changing behavior or reactions requires examining and updating underlying mental models.

deep_dives.research_question: Can an intervention on a stored representation, isolated from input information and output formatting, be shown to change downstream behavior more durably than output-level constraints?
deep_dives.topic: The mental-model layer as a first-class, inspectable artifact
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Mental models are described as the constructed artifact mediating memory, experience, and incoming information
deep_dives.video_title: Systems Thinking: A Little Film About a Big Idea | Introduction to Cabrera Research Lab
deep_dives.why: Locates the correct intervention point for agent behavior change at the persistent internal representation rather than output shaping, and makes representation diffs a maintenance surface with its own eval suite.

evidence_quotes.text: Plugging an electronic device into the wall without realizing the coal-burning grid powering it.
Systems ignorance leads to consistently producing suffering without intending to.

deep_dives.research_question: How to define and measure provenance coverage of an agent's side-effecting actions, and does increasing coverage reduce unintended consequences and improve attribution?
deep_dives.topic: Provenance coverage as a measurable metric for systems awareness
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Define a provenance-coverage metric
deep_dives.video_title: Peter Senge: "Systems Thinking for a Better World" - Aalto Systems Forum 2014
deep_dives.why: Operationalizes systems ignorance as a measurable engineering deficit, enabling detection and remediation of invisible dependencies in agentic systems.

evidence_quotes.text: The word 'nature' is an abstraction that separates humans from the natural world.
Blackfoot Indians have no nouns; their language describes processes, not things ('surfing the flux').

deep_dives.research_question: Does representing agent behavior as event/process flows rather than named components improve multi-step systemic reasoning and coupling visibility?
deep_dives.topic: Process-oriented vs. noun-based representations for agent architecture
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Representation choice, not reasoning power, determines whether coupling is visible.
deep_dives.video_title: Peter Senge: "Systems Thinking for a Better World" - Aalto Systems Forum 2014
deep_dives.why: Tests the claim that representation choice determines what coupling is visible, with direct implications for retry placement, backpressure, and shared state management in agent architectures.

evidence_quotes.text: Undiscovered rework is central to the management of complex projects.
Project dynamics emerge endogenously from interactions between workforce, schedule, tasks, and perceived progress.
halting hiring when projects plateau prematurely

deep_dives.research_question: Can divergence between a self-reported progress signal (tasks marked done, tests passing, agent-declared completion) and an independently verified completion signal be measured online, and does the divergence rate at time T predict rework volume at time T+n?
deep_dives.topic: Online detection of undiscovered rework in agentic and software delivery pipelines
deep_dives.trigger_insight: undiscovered rework is central to the management of complex projects
deep_dives.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson
deep_dives.why: If control decisions (add agents, raise parallelism, halt hiring) are keyed to perceived progress, hidden rework accumulates invisibly and surfaces only as late-stage overrun. A dual-signal instrument turns 'undiscovered' rework into a measurable stock with a leading indicator, which is the precondition for any intervention.

evidence_quotes.text: Policies like building low-cost housing or jobs programs can have unintended long-term compensating feedback effects.
a successful jobs program temporarily helps a city, but long-term feedback loops negate the effect

deep_dives.research_question: How can the time constant of a compensating feedback loop be estimated empirically before knowing it, so that evaluation windows for an intervention are set long enough that benefit rankings do not invert?
deep_dives.topic: Evaluation horizons sized to the slowest compensating feedback loop
deep_dives.trigger_insight: short-term measured benefit is an unreliable predictor of steady-state outcome
deep_dives.video_title: Models that Matter – System Dynamics Applications with Impact by George Richardson
deep_dives.why: Short-horizon wins are systematically selected for when compensating loops exist: added capacity, raised timeouts, relaxed thresholds, or added agents all show immediate improvement while the compensating loop erases it later. Without a method for bounding the loop timescale, benchmark duration is chosen by convenience and the ranking of interventions is wrong.

evidence_quotes.text: Open-loop thinking assumes a linear path (identify problem, gather data, evaluate alternatives, select solution, implement).
Linear project management frameworks (open-loop thinking) consistently fail in complex environments.
Knowing static rules (stay on the right) is insufficient without real-time feedback.

deep_dives.research_question: On long-horizon tasks with external state change, how much reliability does an explicit Goals → Decisions → State → Side Effects → Actions-of-Others loop buy over a fixed plan-then-execute pipeline, and at what cost per completed task?
deep_dives.topic: Closing the loop: state observation as the missing component in agent harnesses
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Open-loop thinking assumes a linear path
deep_dives.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview
deep_dives.why: Most agent harnesses are open-loop pipelines: plan once, call tools, emit an artifact. If the claim that linear frameworks 'consistently fail in complex environments' holds for agents, the primary architectural fix is a state-estimation step whose output feeds the next decision, plus first-class modeling of external actors. This is testable by measuring regression frequency and cost per task across loop variants rather than by arguing about model capability.

evidence_quotes.text: Side effects are simply effects outside our mental model that feed back into the system.
Decisions made without accounting for feedback loops lead to unanticipated long-term consequences.

deep_dives.research_question: Given an explicitly declared agent model boundary, can causally-adjacent but unobserved effects (downstream consumers, cost, rate limits, other systems' state) be enumerated and instrumented so feedback is detected before it compounds into an unexplained failure?
deep_dives.topic: Model boundary as risk surface: instrumenting effects the agent cannot see
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Side effects are simply effects outside our mental model that feed back into the system.
deep_dives.video_title: Introduction to System Dynamics: Overview
deep_dives.why: If side effects are defined as effects outside the model that feed back into the system, then the model boundary is the risk surface and the engineering lever is where the boundary is drawn and instrumented. This converts 'watch out for unintended consequences' into a concrete requirement: observability scope must strictly exceed the agent's reasoning scope, with the gap explicitly instrumented rather than left to surface as a mystery incident.

evidence_quotes.text: Organizational capability behaves like any financial asset or stock: it takes time to build and erodes if neglected over long periods.
Capability does not change right away when investments are turned on or off.
Manufacturing plants firing maintenance mechanics will not see equipment break tomorrow, but capability will slowly erode over time.
Short-term success metrics can be misleading indicators of long-term health.

deep_dives.research_question: Can capability stock (eval coverage, observability depth, maintenance debt, reliability margin) be quantified as a measurable leading indicator that predicts delayed performance collapse before it becomes visible in output metrics?
deep_dives.topic: Measuring capability stock and erosion as leading indicators in AI engineering
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Organizational capability behaves like a stock: it builds through investment and erodes when neglected
deep_dives.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning
deep_dives.why: Organizations cannot protect a capability they cannot see eroding. Without instrumentation for capability stock, the tradeoff between production work and capability development remains invisible and defaults to production.

evidence_quotes.text: Implementing new capabilities always results in worse performance before better performance occurs.
Attempting to fix everything at once deepens the initial performance dip.
Organizations should make small, consistent capability gains part of daily work rather than episodic major transformations.
Software teams failing when trying to adopt entire new operating systems or massive software upgrades all at once.

deep_dives.research_question: What diagnostic criteria separate the expected temporary performance decline of a legitimate capability adoption from the symptoms of an implementation that will never recover?
deep_dives.topic: Distinguishing a necessary worse-before-better adoption dip from a failed implementation
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Adopting new capabilities follows a worse-before-better dynamic
deep_dives.video_title: Useful Doesn't Always Mean Used - Webinar with Nelson Repenning
deep_dives.why: Teams abandon beneficial changes because they cannot tell a learning dip from a failure. This is the core decision point that determines whether new AI frameworks, memory systems, or architectures survive adoption.

evidence_quotes.text: Open-source and proprietary models alike pose cybersecurity threats if malicious actors leverage them.
Enterprises relying on Chinese open-source models or proprietary defenses during security breaches.

deep_dives.research_question: How should model provenance, jurisdiction, and adversarial-reuse potential be quantified and incorporated into enterprise model selection alongside capability and cost, and what evidence exists on relative offensive capability of open-weight versus closed models?

deep_dives.trigger_insight: Model provenance is treated as an enterprise attack surface

deep_dives.why: Model choice is usually optimized on capability and price; treating provenance as an attack surface adds supply-chain, geopolitical, and adversarial-reuse risk to procurement, hosting, and evaluation harnesses.

evidence_quotes.text: There are two major challenges: the potential of a loss-of-control accident and the fear of extreme power concentration.

deep_dives.research_question: How do technical safety mitigations for accident containment interact with governance and access-distribution mechanisms for power concentration, and can the two risk axes be evaluated independently or do they require coupled design?
deep_dives.topic: Bifurcated AI risk: loss-of-control versus concentration of power
deep_dives.trigger_insight: The risk model is bifurcated into loss-of-control accidents versus concentration of power
deep_dives.video_title: Marc Benioff & Sam Altman | Dreamforce 2026

deep_dives.trigger_insight: Rust proved to be very good for agents fairly quickly when effort was put into it
deep_dives.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux
deep_dives.why: If compile-time and type guarantees suppress a class of runtime failures in long-running tool-calling loops where recovery is expensive, then harness language is not a neutral choice and should be evaluated as a reliability variable, not a performance one.

evidence_quotes.text: Focus on co-designing models and harnesses together.
Open source forces companies to compete at the model and harness layers.

deep_dives.research_question: When harness-specific context formats and tool schemas are allowed to deviate from a stable model API contract, do joint model+harness evaluations improve enough to justify the loss of interface stability?
deep_dives.topic: Model-harness co-design versus a stable model API contract
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Focus on co-designing models and harnesses together
deep_dives.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux
deep_dives.why: Co-design implies harness changes can force model-side changes and vice versa, breaking the assumption of a stable contract between model and orchestration layer. Without a joint scoring harness, teams cannot tell whether co-evolution gains exceed the integration cost they impose.

evidence_quotes.text: Open source forces companies to compete at the model and harness layers.
Open-sourcing the CLI, SDK, and app server builds community and contributor engagement.
There are downsides to open source, such as handling random contributions and copycat tools.

deep_dives.research_question: Does open-sourcing a CLI/SDK/app server measurably erode differentiation at the client layer and shift engineering investment toward the model and harness layers, or does it mainly convert client tooling into an unowned maintenance burden?
deep_dives.topic: What open-sourcing the client layer actually commoditizes
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Open source forces companies to compete at the model and harness layers
deep_dives.video_title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux
deep_dives.why: It inverts the usual assumption that client tooling is the moat. If the interface layer is commoditized, investment must concentrate where switching costs actually live — context assembly, tool orchestration and execution loop — otherwise the product is replicable.

evidence_quotes.text: GPT-6 Astra recreated Manhattan street-by-street from a simple text prompt in one week
Astra generating high-fidelity models of Manhattan and populated agent worlds

deep_dives.research_question: Can a text-prompt world generator produce reproducible synthetic environments whose specified difficulty is monotonically related to measured agent performance, and what seeded snapshot semantics are required to make generated worlds as dependable as hand-built benchmarks?
deep_dives.topic: Environment-generation APIs for agent evaluation
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Astra generating high-fidelity models of Manhattan and populated agent worlds
deep_dives.video_title: Jensen Says “AGI Has Arrived,” OpenAI Agents Hijack a German Website, & OpenAI Solves Navier-Stokes
deep_dives.why: If high-fidelity worlds like Manhattan can be generated from a prompt, agent evaluation becomes an environment-generation problem rather than a static fixture problem, enabling adversarially varied and reproducible scenarios.

evidence_quotes.text: Omar Khattab's DSPy-based RLM prototype for summarizing arbitrarily long documents.
Delegates to sub-LMs as functions inside a REPL.

deep_dives.research_question: How do sub-LM signature granularity, typing, and contract design in a DSPy-based RLM affect recursion depth, total call count, and final answer accuracy?
deep_dives.topic: Sub-LM signature design in DSPy and its effect on recursion quality
deep_dives.trigger_insight: What are the best practices for structuring sub-LM signatures in DSPy?
deep_dives.video_title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners
deep_dives.why: The sub-LM interface is the new critical path; without design guidance, practitioners will rediscover suboptimal patterns by trial and error.

evidence_quotes.text: Telepathy implant allowing users to play video games by thinking.
Restoring full body mobility by bypassing spinal injuries.

deep_dives.research_question: When is bypassing a degraded subsystem with a parallel high-bandwidth channel preferable to in-place repair, and how should the new channel be hardened?
